sentences.zh: 丘靈鞠

translations.literal: Qiu Lingju
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Lingju

sentences.zh: 丘靈鞠，吳興烏程人也。

translations.literal: Qiu Lingju was a native of Wucheng in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Lingju was from Wucheng in Wuxing commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖系，祕書監。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xi was Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xi had served as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 靈鞠少好學，善屬文。

translations.literal: Lingju from youth loved learning and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: From his youth Lingju loved study and excelled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 與上計，仕郡爲吏。

translations.literal: He went up with the annual tribute report and served in the commandery as a clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the annual tribute delegation to the capital and took a post as a commandery clerk.

sentences.zh: 州辟從事，詣領軍沈演之。

translations.literal: The province recruited him as an aide and he went to call on the General of the Vanguard Shen Yanzi.
translations.idiomatic: The province appointed him as an aide, and he paid a visit to Shen Yanzi, General of the Vanguard.

sentences.zh: 演之曰：「身昔爲州職，詣領軍謝晦，賔主坐處，政如今日。

translations.literal: Yanzi said: "I myself once held a provincial post and went to call on Xie Hui, General of the Vanguard; the seating of host and guest was exactly as today.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzi said, "When I was a provincial official I once called on Xie Hui, General of the Vanguard—the arrangement of host and guest was just as it is today.

sentences.zh: 卿將來或復如此也。」

translations.literal: You in the future may again be like this.
translations.idiomatic: You may find yourself in the same position someday."

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，爲州主簿。

translations.literal: He was recommended as a Cultivated Talent and made provincial chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He was recommended as Cultivated Talent and appointed provincial chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 累遷員外郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to External Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to External Attendant.

sentences.zh: 宋孝武殷貴妃亡，靈鞠獻輓歌詩三首，云「雲橫廣階闇，霜深高殿寒」。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Song's honored consort Yin died, Lingju presented three dirge poems, saying "Clouds spread across the broad steps in darkness, frost lies deep and the high halls grow cold."
translations.idiomatic: After the death of Emperor Xiaowu's honored consort Yin, Lingju submitted three dirge poems including the lines, "Clouds spread across the broad terrace in gloom; deep frost chills the lofty hall."

sentences.zh: 帝擿句嗟賞。

translations.literal: The emperor picked out lines and sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor singled out certain lines and praised them with admiration.

sentences.zh: 除新安王北中郎參軍，出爲剡烏程令，不得志。

translations.literal: He was appointed aide to the Prince of Xin'an, Northern Army General of the Center, went out as magistrate of Yan and Wucheng, and was discontent.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed aide to the Prince of Xin'an as Northern Army General of the Center, then sent out as magistrate of Yan and Wucheng, where he found no fulfillment.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，坐東賊黨錮數年。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi he was confined for years on account of affiliation with the eastern rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Taishi era he was imprisoned for several years as an associate of the eastern rebels.

sentences.zh: 褚淵爲吳興，謂人曰：「此郡才士，唯有丘靈鞠及沈勃耳。」

translations.literal: Chu Yuan was [prefect of] Wuxing and said to people: "The talented men of this commandery are only Qiu Lingju and Shen Bo."
translations.idiomatic: When Chu Yuan served as prefect of Wuxing, he told others, "The only true men of talent in this commandery are Qiu Lingju and Shen Bo."

sentences.zh: 乃啓申之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he memorialized recommending him.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial recommending him.

sentences.zh: 明帝使著《大駕南討紀論》。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming had him compose "A Recorded Discussion of the Imperial Campaign South."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming had him write the Recorded Discussion of the Imperial Southern Campaign.

sentences.zh: 久之，除太尉參軍，轉安北記室，帶扶風太守，不就。

translations.literal: After a long while he was appointed aide to the Grand Commander, transferred to secretary of the Army Pacifying the North, concurrently Grand Prefect of Fufeng, but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed aide to the Grand Commander, then transferred to secretary under the Army Pacifying the North with concurrent appointment as Grand Prefect of Fufeng, which he declined.

sentences.zh: 爲尚書三公郎，建康令，轉通直郎，兼中書郎。

translations.literal: He served as a Three Excellencies' attendant in the Ministry of Works, magistrate of Jiankang, transferred to Direct Attendant, and concurrently Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a Three Excellencies' attendant in the Ministry of Works, then as magistrate of Jiankang, and was later transferred to Direct Attendant with concurrent appointment as Secretariat Attendant.

sentences.zh: 昇明中，遷正員郎，領本郡中正，兼中書郎如故。

translations.literal: During Shengming he was promoted to Regular Attendant, headed the commandery impartial selector of his native place, and concurrently was Secretariat Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shengming era he was promoted to Regular Attendant, appointed head impartial selector for his native commandery, and retained his concurrent post as Secretariat Attendant.

sentences.zh: 時方禪讓，太祖使靈鞠參掌詔策。

translations.literal: At the time the abdication was underway; the Founding Emperor had Lingju share in managing edicts and proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: During the impending transfer of the throne, the Founding Emperor put Lingju in charge of drafting imperial edicts and proclamations.

sentences.zh: 建元元年，轉中書郎，中正如故，敕知東宮手筆。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan he was transferred to Secretariat Attendant, impartial selector as before, and ordered to manage the crown prince's personal writings.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianyuan he became Secretariat Attendant while retaining his post as impartial selector, and was ordered to oversee the crown prince's personal writings.

sentences.zh: 尋又掌知國史。

translations.literal: Soon after he also took charge of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was also placed in charge of the national history.

sentences.zh: 明年，出爲鎮南長史、尋陽相，遷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: The next year he went out as chief secretary to the Army Guarding the South and administrator of Xunyang, then was promoted to Left Assistant Minister of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was sent out as chief secretary under the Army Guarding the South and administrator of Xunyang, then promoted to Left Assistant Minister.

sentences.zh: 世祖卽位，轉通直常侍，尋領東觀祭酒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu acceded, he was transferred to Direct Regular Attendant, and soon headed the Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu came to the throne, he was transferred to Direct Regular Attendant and soon appointed Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 靈鞠曰：「久居官不願數遷，使我終身爲祭酒，不恨也。」

translations.literal: Lingju said: "Long in office, I do not wish frequent transfers—let me be libationer for life, and I shall have no regret."
translations.idiomatic: Lingju said, "I have been in office a long time and do not want to keep moving about—if I could spend my whole career as libationer, I would have no regrets."

sentences.zh: 永明二年，領驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongming he headed the Valiant Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongming he was appointed Valiant Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 靈鞠不樂武位，謂人曰：「我應還東掘顧榮冢。

translations.literal: Lingju was not pleased with a military post and said to people: "I ought to go back east and dig up Gu Rong's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Unhappy with a military appointment, Lingju told others, "I ought to go back east and dig up Gu Rong's grave.

sentences.zh: 江南地方數千里，士子風流，皆出此中。

translations.literal: The lands south of the Yangtze extend thousands of li; the refinement of scholar-gentlemen all comes from within this region.
translations.idiomatic: For thousands of li south of the Yangtze, the elegance of cultured gentlemen had all sprung from this country.

sentences.zh: 顧榮忽引諸傖渡，妨我輩塗轍，死有餘罪。」

translations.literal: Gu Rong suddenly led all those northerners across the river, blocking our path; dead, he still had crimes to spare."
translations.idiomatic: Gu Rong suddenly ushered all those crude northerners across the river, blocking the road for the rest of us—even in death his guilt is not exhausted."

sentences.zh: 改正員常侍。

translations.literal: He was changed to Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 靈鞠好飲酒，臧否人物，在沈淵座見王儉詩，淵曰：「王令文章大進。」

translations.literal: Lingju loved wine and praised or condemned people; seated with Shen Yuan he saw Wang Jian's poem, and Yuan said: "Commander Wang's writings have advanced greatly."
translations.idiomatic: Lingju was fond of drink and quick to praise or disparage others. Once at Shen Yuan's table he saw a poem by Wang Jian; Yuan remarked, "Commander Wang's writing has improved enormously."

sentences.zh: 靈鞠曰：「何如我未進時？」

translations.literal: Lingju said: "How does it compare with before I had advanced?"
translations.idiomatic: Lingju replied, "And how does it compare with his work before he improved?"

sentences.zh: 此言達儉。

translations.literal: This remark reached Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Word of this remark reached Jian.

sentences.zh: 靈鞠宋世文名甚盛，入齊頗減。

translations.literal: Lingju's literary fame in the Song was very great; entering Qi it diminished considerably.
translations.idiomatic: Lingju's literary reputation had been very great in the Song, but after the Qi dynasty it declined noticeably.

sentences.zh: 蓬髮弛縱，無形儀，不治家業。

translations.literal: With tangled hair hanging loose, no proper bearing, he did not manage his household estate.
translations.idiomatic: He let his hair hang wild and paid no heed to propriety or household affairs.

sentences.zh: 王儉謂人曰：「丘公仕宦不進，才亦退矣。」

translations.literal: Wang Jian said to people: "Master Qiu's official career has not advanced, and his talent has also declined."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian told others, "Master Qiu's official career has not advanced—and neither has his talent."

sentences.zh: 遷長沙王車騎長史，太中大夫，卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to chief secretary to the Prince of Changsha's Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Master of Palace Counsel, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to chief secretary to the Prince of Changsha as General of Chariots and Cavalry, then Grand Master of Palace Counsel, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 著《江左文章錄序》，起太興，訖元熙。

translations.literal: He authored the Preface to "A Catalogue of Writings of the Eastern Region," from Taixing through Yuanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Preface to A Catalogue of Writings from the Eastern Region, covering the period from Taixing to Yuanxi.

sentences.zh: 文集行於世。

translations.literal: His collected writings circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works circulated in his time.

sentences.zh: 檀超

translations.literal: Tan Chao
translations.idiomatic: Tan Chao

sentences.zh: 檀超字悅祖，高平金郷人也。

translations.literal: Tan Chao, courtesy name Yuezu, was a native of Jinxiang in Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Chao, courtesy name Yuezu, was from Jinxiang in Gaoping commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖弘宗，宋南琅邪太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hongzong was Grand Administrator of Southern Langye in the Song.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hongzong had served as Grand Administrator of Southern Langye under the Song.

sentences.zh: 超少好文學，放誕任氣，解褐州西曹。

translations.literal: Chao from youth loved literature, was unrestrained and defiant by temperament, and began his career as western bureau clerk of the province.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Chao loved literature; wild and defiant by nature, he entered service as western bureau clerk for the province.

sentences.zh: 嘗與別駕蕭惠開共事，不爲之下。

translations.literal: He once served together with the Administration Aide Xiao Huikai and would not rank below him.
translations.idiomatic: Once when serving alongside the Administration Aide Xiao Huikai, he refused to defer to him.

sentences.zh: 謂惠開曰：「我與卿俱起一老姥，何足相誇？」

translations.literal: He said to Huikai: "You and I both rose through one old woman—what is there to boast about to each other?"
translations.idiomatic: He told Huikai, "You and I both owe our advancement to the same old woman—what is there for either of us to boast about?"

sentences.zh: 蕭太后，惠開之祖姑，長沙王道憐妃，超祖姑也。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xiao was Huikai's great-aunt, consort of the Prince of Changsha, Prince Dao of Lian, and Chao's great-aunt.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xiao—Huikai's grandaunt, consort of the Prince of Changsha Dao of Lian—was also Chao's grandaunt.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才。

translations.literal: He was recommended as Cultivated Talent.
translations.idiomatic: He was recommended as Cultivated Talent.

sentences.zh: 孝建初，坐事徙梁州，板宣威府參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojian he was banished to Liangzhou for an offense and was appointed aide on the staff of the General Establishing Prestige.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Xiaojian era he was exiled to Liangzhou for an offense and appointed aide on the staff of the General Establishing Prestige.

sentences.zh: 孝武聞超有文章，敕還直東宮，除驃騎參軍、寧蠻主簿，鎮北諮議。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu heard that Chao had literary talent, ordered him back to attend the Eastern Palace, and appointed him aide to the Rapid Cavalry General, chief clerk of Pacifying the Barbarians, and adviser to the Army Pacifying the North.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu learned of Chao's literary gifts, he ordered him recalled to serve at the Eastern Palace and appointed him aide to the Rapid Cavalry General, chief clerk of Pacifying the Barbarians, and adviser under the Army Pacifying the North.

sentences.zh: 超累佐蕃職，不得志，轉尚書度支郎，車騎功曹，桂陽內史。

translations.literal: Chao repeatedly assisted in princely posts without satisfaction, transferred to revenue section attendant in the Ministry of Works, merit recorder for Chariots and Cavalry, and interior administrator of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated stints on princely staffs left him frustrated, he was transferred to revenue attendant in the Ministry of Works, then to merit recorder for the General of Chariots and Cavalry and interior administrator of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 入爲殿中郎，兼中書郎，零陵內史，征北驃騎記室，國子博士，兼左丞。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as palace attendant, concurrently Secretariat attendant, interior administrator of Lingling, secretary to the Northern Expedition Rapid Cavalry General, National University erudite, and concurrently left assistant minister.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital as palace attendant and concurrent Secretariat attendant, then served as interior administrator of Lingling, secretary to the Northern Expedition Rapid Cavalry General, National University erudite, and concurrent left assistant minister.

sentences.zh: 超嗜酒，好言詠，舉止和靡，自比晉郗超，爲「高平二超」。

translations.literal: Chao was addicted to wine, loved reciting and composing poetry, his bearing soft and indulgent; he compared himself to Xi Chao of Jin and called themselves "the two Chaos of Gaoping."
translations.idiomatic: Chao was devoted to wine and fond of verse; soft and unhurried in manner, he likened himself to Xi Chao of the Jin and spoke of "the two Chaos of Gaoping."

sentences.zh: 謂人曰：「猶覺我爲優也。」

translations.literal: He said to people: "I still feel that I am the superior one."
translations.idiomatic: He told others, "I still think I come out ahead."

sentences.zh: 太祖賞愛之。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor prized and favored him.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor valued and favored him.

sentences.zh: 遷驍騎將軍，常侍，司徒右長史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Valiant Cavalry General, Regular Attendant, and right chief secretary to the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Valiant Cavalry General, Regular Attendant, and right chief secretary under the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 建元二年，初置史官，以超與驃騎記室江淹掌史職。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyuan, when historiographers were first established, Chao and Jiang Yan, secretary to the Rapid Cavalry General, were put in charge of historical duties.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianyuan, when official historiographers were first appointed, Chao and Jiang Yan, secretary to the Rapid Cavalry General, were assigned to oversee the history project.

sentences.zh: 上表立條例，開元紀號，不取宋年。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial establishing regulations, using the Jianyuan era designation and not adopting Song reign years.
translations.idiomatic: They submitted a memorial proposing institutional rules: the history would adopt the Jianyuan reign designation and would not use Song era names.

sentences.zh: 封爵各詳本傳，無假年表。

translations.literal: Enfeoffments and titles would each be detailed in their respective biographies, with no need for a chronological table.
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffments and titles would each be treated fully in the relevant biographies, without relying on a chronological table.

sentences.zh: 立十志：《律曆》、《禮樂》、《天文》、《五行》、《郊祀》、《刑法》、《藝文》依班固，《朝會》、《輿服》依蔡邕、司馬彪，《州郡》依徐爰。

translations.literal: Ten treatises were to be established: "Calendar and Chronology," "Rites and Music," "Astronomy," "The Five Elements," "Suburban Sacrifices," and "Penal Law" and "Arts and Literature" following Ban Gu; "Court Assemblies" and "Chariots and Vestments" following Cai Yong and Sima Biao; "Provinces and Commanderies" following Xu Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ten treatises were proposed—Calendar and Chronology, Rites and Music, Astronomy, the Five Elements, Suburban Sacrifices, Penal Law, and Arts and Literature following Ban Gu; Court Assemblies and Chariots and Vestments following Cai Yong and Sima Biao; and Provinces and Commanderies following Xu Yuan.

sentences.zh: 《百官》依范曄，合《州郡》。

translations.literal: "Officials" following Fan Ye, combined with "Provinces and Commanderies."
translations.idiomatic: Officials would follow Fan Ye's model and be combined with Provinces and Commanderies.

sentences.zh: 班固五星載《天文》，日蝕載《五行》；

translations.literal: Ban Gu placed the five planets in "Astronomy" and solar eclipses in "The Five Elements";
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu had placed the five planets in Astronomy and solar eclipses in the Five Elements treatise;

sentences.zh: 改日蝕入《天文志》。

translations.literal: eclipses were to be changed to enter the "Astronomical Treatise."
translations.idiomatic: they proposed moving solar eclipses into the Astronomical Treatise.

sentences.zh: 以建元爲始。

translations.literal: Jianyuan was to be taken as the beginning.
translations.idiomatic: The history would begin with the Jianyuan era.

sentences.zh: 帝女體自皇宗，立傳以備甥舅之重。

translations.literal: Imperial daughters by nature descend from the imperial clan; establishing a biography was to provide for the weight of relations by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Because imperial daughters spring from the imperial clan, separate biographies would be established to give due weight to affinal kinship.

sentences.zh: 又立《處士》、《列女》傳。

translations.literal: Also to establish "Reclusive Scholars" and "Exemplary Women" biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Biographies of Reclusive Scholars and Exemplary Women would also be added.

sentences.zh: 詔內外詳議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered detailed discussion inside and outside the court.
translations.idiomatic: An edict called for detailed deliberation within and outside the court.

sentences.zh: 左僕射王儉議：「金粟之重，八政所先，食貨通則國富民實，宜加編錄，以崇務本。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Wang Jian argued: "The weight of grain and gold is what the eight duties put first; when food and goods circulate, the state grows rich and the people grow full—this ought to be added to the record to honor devotion to fundamentals.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Wang Jian argued: "Grain and treasure come first among the eight great duties of government; when food and currency flow freely, the state grows rich and the people secure. A treatise on food and goods ought to be added to honor attention to fundamentals.

sentences.zh: 《朝會志》前史不書，蔡邕稱先師胡廣說《漢舊儀》，此乃伯喈一家之意，曲碎小儀，无煩錄。

translations.literal: "Court Assemblies" previous histories did not record; Cai Yong spoke of his late teacher Hu Guang's exposition of "Han Old Protocols"—this was Bo'e's personal view, petty minor ceremonies not worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: Previous histories had not included a Court Assemblies treatise; Cai Yong had merely cited his teacher Hu Guang on Han court protocol—this was one man's opinion, concerned with trivial ceremonial minutiae not worth recording.

sentences.zh: 宜立《食貨》，省《朝會》。

translations.literal: It is appropriate to establish "Food and Goods" and omit "Court Assemblies."
translations.idiomatic: A Food and Goods treatise should be established in place of Court Assemblies.

sentences.zh: 《洪範》九疇，一曰五行。

translations.literal: The "Great Plan's" nine categories—the first is the Five Elements.
translations.idiomatic: The nine divisions of the Great Plan begin with the Five Elements.

sentences.zh: 五行之本，先乎水火之精，是爲日月五行之宗也。

translations.literal: The root of the Five Elements lies first in the essences of water and fire; these are the source of the sun, moon, and Five Elements.
translations.idiomatic: The foundation of the Five Elements lies in the essences of water and fire—they are the source of the sun, moon, and the five elemental forces.

sentences.zh: 今宜憲章前軌，無所改革。

translations.literal: Now one should take the statutes of former models as law, with no reforms.
translations.idiomatic: The existing arrangement should follow precedent without change.

sentences.zh: 又立《帝女傳》，亦非淺識所安。

translations.literal: Also establishing an "Imperial Daughters" biography is not what shallow understanding can accept.
translations.idiomatic: Nor would a separate treatise on imperial daughters sit well with sober judgment.

sentences.zh: 若有高德異行，自當載在《列女》，若止於常美，則仍舊不書。」

translations.literal: If there are lofty virtue and unusual conduct, they should naturally be entered in "Exemplary Women"; if only ordinary excellence, then as before do not record."
translations.idiomatic: Women of exceptional virtue and conduct belong in Exemplary Women; those of merely ordinary worth should, as before, go unrecorded."

sentences.zh: 詔：「日月災隷《天文》，餘如儉議。」

translations.literal: Edict: "Calamities of sun and moon belong under Astronomy; the rest as Jian argued."
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "Solar and lunar portents shall fall under Astronomy; the rest accords with Jian's proposal."

sentences.zh: 超史功未就，卒官。

translations.literal: Chao's historical work was not completed; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Chao died in office before the history could be finished.

sentences.zh: 江淹撰成之，猶不備也。

translations.literal: Jiang Yan compiled and completed it, yet it was still not complete.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yan completed the draft, but it remained incomplete.

sentences.zh: 時豫章熊襄著《齊典》，上起十代。

translations.literal: At the time Xiong Xiang of Yuzhang authored "Qi Canon," beginning ten generations back.
translations.idiomatic: Around this time Xiong Xiang of Yuzhang composed the Qi Canon, tracing back ten generations.

sentences.zh: 其序云：「《尚書》《堯典》，謂之《虞書》，則附所述，故通謂之齊，名爲《河洛金匱》。」

translations.literal: Its preface says: "The 'Canon of Yao' in the Documents is called the 'Book of Yu'—thus attached to what is narrated, so commonly called Qi, titled 'River Luo Golden Coffer.'"
translations.idiomatic: Its preface states: "The Canon of Yao in the Documents is called the Book of Yu; because it attaches to the narrative at hand, the work as a whole may be called Qi, and it is titled Golden Coffer of the River Luo."

sentences.zh: 卞彬

translations.literal: Bian Bin
translations.idiomatic: Bian Bin

sentences.zh: 卞彬字士蔚，濟陰冤句人也。

translations.literal: Bian Bin, courtesy name Shiwei, was a native of Yuanqu in Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Bin, courtesy name Shiwei, was from Yuanqu in Jiyin commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖嗣之，中領軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sizhi was General of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sizhi had served as General of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 父延之，有剛氣，爲上虞令。

translations.literal: His father Yanzhi had a stern spirit and served as magistrate of Shangyu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yanzhi was a man of strong character who served as magistrate of Shangyu.

sentences.zh: 彬才操不羣，文多指刺。

translations.literal: Bin's talent and conduct were unmatched; his writings often pointed and stabbed.
translations.idiomatic: Bin's talent and conduct were extraordinary; his writings were often biting satire.

sentences.zh: 州辟西曹主簿，奉朝請，員外郎。

translations.literal: The province recruited him as western bureau chief clerk, court gentleman in attendance, and external attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The province appointed him western bureau chief clerk, then court gentleman in attendance and external attendant.

sentences.zh: 宋元徽末，四貴輔政。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanhui in the Song, the four nobles assisted in government.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuanhui era, the four powerful nobles dominated the government.

sentences.zh: 彬謂太祖曰：「外閒有童謠云：『可憐可念尸著服，孝子不在日代哭，列管蹔鳴死滅族。』

translations.literal: Bin said to the Founding Emperor: "Outside there is a children's rhyme saying: 'Pitiable, lamentable—a corpse in mourning dress; the filial son is not present, the sun replaces weeping; the row of pipes sounds briefly and the clan is destroyed.'
translations.idiomatic: Bin told the Founding Emperor, "There is a popular rhyme abroad that runs: 'Pitiable, lamentable—a corpse in mourning garb; the filial son is absent, the sun stands in for tears; the pipes sound briefly and the clan is annihilated.'

sentences.zh: 公頗聞不？」

translations.literal: Have you perhaps heard it, sir?"
translations.idiomatic: Have you heard it, sir?"

sentences.zh: 時王蘊居父憂，與袁粲同死，故云尸著服也。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Yun was in mourning for his father and died with Yuan Can, hence "corpse in mourning dress."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun was then in mourning for his father and died with Yuan Can—hence the line about a corpse in mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 服者衣也，褚字邊衣也，孝除子，以日代者，謂褚淵也。

translations.literal: "Dress" means clothing; beside the character for Chu is the clothing radical; "filial" removes "son"; "sun replaces" refers to Chu Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: "Dress" (fu) means garment—the radical for garment appears beside the character for Chu; "filial" (xiao) minus "son" (zi); and "sun replaces" (ri dai) pointed to Chu Yuan.

sentences.zh: 列管，蕭也。」

translations.literal: "Row of pipes" means Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: "Row of pipes" (lie guan) referred to the Xiao clan.

sentences.zh: 彬退，太祖笑曰：「彬自作此。」

translations.literal: Bin withdrew; the Founding Emperor laughed and said: "Bin composed this himself."
translations.idiomatic: When Bin withdrew, the Founding Emperor laughed and said, "Bin made that rhyme up himself."

sentences.zh: 齊臺初建，彬又曰：「誰謂宋遠，跂予望之。」

translations.literal: When the Qi regime was first established, Bin again said: "Who says Song is far? I stand on tiptoe gazing toward it."
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi regime was first established, Bin quoted the ode: "Who says Song is far? I stand on tiptoe and gaze toward it."

sentences.zh: 太祖聞之，不加罪也。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor heard it and did not impose punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor heard this but imposed no punishment.

sentences.zh: 除右軍參軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed aide to the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed aide to the Right Army.

sentences.zh: 家貧，出爲南康郡丞。

translations.literal: His family was poor; he went out as assistant magistrate of Nankang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Poor at home, he was sent out as assistant magistrate of Nankang commandery.

sentences.zh: 彬頗飲酒，擯棄形骸。

translations.literal: Bin drank considerably and cast off bodily form.
translations.idiomatic: Bin drank heavily and cared nothing for propriety or bodily comfort.

sentences.zh: 作《蚤虱賦序》曰：「余居貧，布衣十年不制。

translations.literal: He composed the preface to "Ode to Fleas and Lice," saying: "I dwell in poverty; plain cloth garments for ten years without making new ones.
translations.idiomatic: In the preface to his Ode to Fleas and Lice he wrote: "I live in poverty; for ten years I have worn the same homespun coat without making a new one.

sentences.zh: 一袍之縕，有生所託，資其寒暑，無與易之。

translations.literal: One robe's worn padding—a lifetime's reliance; relying on it for cold and heat, nothing with which to exchange it.
translations.idiomatic: This single padded robe is all I have to rely on for shelter from heat and cold; I have nothing to replace it.

sentences.zh: 爲人多病，起居甚疏，縈寢敗絮，不能自釋。

translations.literal: As a person I am often ill; my daily rising and resting are very careless; tangled bedding of ruined cotton, unable to release myself from it.
translations.idiomatic: I am sickly by nature, careless in my daily habits, and tangled in bedding of rotted cotton stuffing that I cannot shake off.

sentences.zh: 兼攝性懈惰，嬾事皮膚，澡刷不謹，澣沐失時，四體，加以臭穢，故葦席蓬纓之間，蚤虱猥流。

translations.literal: Moreover my nature is slack and lazy; I neglect the care of skin; bathing and scrubbing are not careful, washing and bathing miss their times; the four limbs, moreover foul and filthy—therefore between rush mat and hemp cap tassels, fleas and lice swarm in profusion.
translations.idiomatic: My nature is also slack and lazy; I neglect my skin, bathe and scrub carelessly, and wash at the wrong times. My four limbs, moreover, grow foul and rank, so that fleas and lice swarm between my rush mat and hemp cap cord.

sentences.zh: 淫癢渭濩，無時恕肉，探揣擭撮，日不替手。

translations.literal: Excessive itching surges and swells; there is no time to spare the flesh; probing, groping, pinching, and picking—day after day the hands never rest.
translations.idiomatic: Itching runs wild without respite; there is never a moment's relief for my flesh. I probe, grope, pinch, and pick at myself, and my hands never idle for a day.

sentences.zh: 虱有諺言，朝生暮孫。

translations.literal: Lice have a proverb: born in the morning, grandchildren by evening.
translations.idiomatic: There is a saying about lice: born in the morning, with grandchildren by evening.

sentences.zh: 若吾之虱者，無湯沐之慮，絕相弔之憂，宴聚乎久襟爛布之裳，服無改換，搯齧不能加，脫略緩嬾，復不懃於捕討，孫孫息息，三十五歲焉。」

translations.literal: As for lice like mine: no worry of hot baths, utterly cut off from mutual condolence; they feast and gather on the long-collared, rotted-cloth robe; clothes without change or replacement; biting and gnawing cannot increase; careless, slack, and lazy, again not diligent in capture and extermination—generation after generation at ease, thirty-five years indeed."
translations.idiomatic: But lice like mine need never fear hot baths or mourn one another's deaths. They feast on my long-collared robe of rotted cloth, which never changes; biting and gnawing do them no harm. Careless and lazy, I am not diligent in hunting them down, so generation after generation they live at ease—for thirty-five years now."

sentences.zh: 其略言皆實錄也。

translations.literal: The gist of his remarks was all factual record.
translations.idiomatic: The gist of what he wrote was entirely true.

sentences.zh: 除南海王國郎中令，尚書比部郎，安吉令，車騎記室。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Secretariat of the Principality of Nanhai, Gentleman of the Ministry of Justice Comparison Section, Magistrate of Anji, and Recorder of the Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Director of the Secretariat of the Principality of Nanhai, Gentleman of the Ministry of Justice Comparison Section, magistrate of Anji, and recorder for the Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 彬性好飲酒，以瓠壺瓢勺杬皮爲肴，著帛冠十二年不改易，以大瓠爲火籠，什物多諸詭異。

translations.literal: Bin by nature loved drinking wine; he used gourd pots, ladles, spoons, and elm bark as food; he wore a cloth cap for twelve years without changing it; he used a large gourd as a brazier; his utensils were mostly strange and odd.
translations.idiomatic: Bin loved wine by nature. He ate from gourd pots, ladles, spoons, and elm bark, wore the same cloth cap for twelve years without changing it, used a large gourd as a brazier, and kept many bizarre household things.

sentences.zh: 自稱「卞田居」，婦爲「傅蠶室」。

translations.literal: He styled himself "Bian the Field Dweller," and called his wife "Mistress of the Silkworm Room."
translations.idiomatic: He styled himself "Bian the Field Dweller," and called his wife "Mistress of the Silkworm Room."

sentences.zh: 或諫曰：「卿都不持操，名器何由得升？」

translations.literal: Someone admonished him, saying: "You maintain no conduct at all—how can you rise to honored office?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone admonished him, saying, "You keep no standards of conduct at all—how can you rise to honored office?"

sentences.zh: 彬曰：「擲五木子，十擲輙鞬，豈復是擲子之拙。

translations.literal: Bin said: "When I throw the five gaming tiles, every ten throws I always win the full set—is that still the clumsiness of the thrower?
translations.idiomatic: Bin replied, "When I throw the five gaming tiles, I win the full set every ten throws—is that still the thrower's clumsiness?

sentences.zh: 吾好擲，政極此耳。」

translations.literal: I love throwing; this is exactly the limit of it."
translations.idiomatic: I love to throw—that is all there is to it."

sentences.zh: 永元中，爲平越長史、綏建太守，卒官。

translations.literal: In the Yongyuan era he served as Chief Administrator of Pingyue and Administrator of Suijian, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongyuan era he served as chief administrator of Pingyue and administrator of Suijian, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 彬又目禽獸云：「羊性淫而狠，豬性卑而率，鵝性頑而傲，狗性險而出。」

translations.literal: Bin also categorized birds and beasts, saying: "Sheep by nature are lustful and fierce; pigs by nature are base and straightforward; geese by nature are stubborn and proud; dogs by nature are treacherous and outward-going."
translations.idiomatic: Bin also described birds and beasts, saying, "Sheep are lustful and fierce by nature; pigs are base and blunt; geese are stubborn and proud; dogs are treacherous and outward-going."

sentences.zh: 皆指斥貴勢。

translations.literal: All were aimed at denouncing the powerful and eminent.
translations.idiomatic: All of these were aimed at denouncing the powerful and eminent.

sentences.zh: 其蝦蟆賦云：「紆青拖紫，名爲蛤魚。」

translations.literal: In his Rhapsody on the Toad he wrote: "Wrapped in green and trailing purple, its name is frog-fish."
translations.idiomatic: In his Rhapsody on the Toad he wrote, "Wrapped in green and trailing purple, its name is frog-fish."

sentences.zh: 世謂比令僕也。

translations.literal: The world took this as a comparison to the Director of Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: People took this as a satire on the Director of Attendants.

sentences.zh: 又云：「科斗唯唯，羣浮闇水。

translations.literal: He also wrote: "Tadpoles bob and nod, floating in crowds in dark water.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote, "Tadpoles bob and nod, floating in crowds in dark water.

sentences.zh: 維朝繼夕，聿役如鬼。」

translations.literal: From morning through evening, serving like ghosts."
translations.idiomatic: From morning through evening they serve like ghosts."

sentences.zh: 比令史諮事也。

translations.literal: This was a comparison to the clerks who handled consultations.
translations.idiomatic: This was taken as a satire on the clerks who handled consultations.

sentences.zh: 文章傳於閭巷。

translations.literal: His writings circulated in the lanes and alleys.
translations.idiomatic: His writings circulated among the common people.

sentences.zh: 永明中，琅邪諸葛勗爲國子生，作《雲中賦》，指祭酒以下，皆有形似之目。

translations.literal: During the Yongming era, Zhuge Mu of Langya, a student at the Imperial University, composed the Rhapsody from the Clouds, assigning to the Chancellor and those below likeness-titles one and all.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongming era, Zhuge Mu of Langya, a student at the Imperial University, wrote the Rhapsody from the Clouds, assigning likeness-titles to the Chancellor and everyone below him.

sentences.zh: 坐繫東冶，作《東冶徒賦》，世祖見，赦之。

translations.literal: For this he was imprisoned in the Eastern Ironworks; he wrote the Rhapsody of an Eastern Ironworks Prisoner; the Emperor saw it and pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was imprisoned in the Eastern Ironworks. He wrote the Rhapsody of an Eastern Ironworks Prisoner, and when the Emperor saw it, he pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 又有陳郡袁嘏，自重其文。

translations.literal: There was also Yuan Gu of Chen commandery, who held his own writings in high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Yuan Gu of Chen commandery, who held his own writings in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 謂人云：「我詩應須大材迮之，不爾飛去。」

translations.literal: He told people: "My poems must be contained in a great vessel; otherwise they would fly away."
translations.idiomatic: He told people, "My poems need a great vessel to hold them; otherwise they would fly away."

sentences.zh: 建武末，爲諸暨令，被王敬則所殺。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jianwu era he served as magistrate of Zhuji and was killed by Wang Jingze.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jianwu era he served as magistrate of Zhuji and was killed by Wang Jingze.

sentences.zh: 丘巨源

translations.literal: Qiu Juyuan
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Juyuan

sentences.zh: 丘巨源，蘭陵蘭陵人也。

translations.literal: Qiu Juyuan was a native of Lanling in Lanling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Juyuan was from Lanling in Lanling commandery.

sentences.zh: 宋初土斷屬丹陽，後屬蘭陵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Song, after the land reallocation he belonged to Danyang; later he belonged to Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Song, after the land reallocation his household belonged to Danyang; later it belonged to Lanling.

sentences.zh: 巨源少舉丹陽郡孝廉，爲宋孝武所知。

translations.literal: Juyuan in youth was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt of Danyang commandery and came to the notice of Emperor Xiaowu of Song.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Juyuan was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt of Danyang commandery and came to the notice of Emperor Xiaowu of Song.

sentences.zh: 大明五人，敕助徐爰撰國史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of the Daming era, he was ordered to assist Xu Ai in compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Daming era, he was ordered to assist Xu Ai in compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，江夏王義恭取爲掌書記。

translations.literal: When the Emperor died, Prince Jiangxia Liu Yigong took him on as chief recorder.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, Prince Jiangxia Liu Yigong took him on as chief recorder.

sentences.zh: 明帝卽位，使參詔誥，引在左右。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming acceded, he had him participate in drafting edicts and proclamations and kept him at his side.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming acceded, he had him participate in drafting edicts and proclamations and kept him at his side.

sentences.zh: 自南臺御史爲王景文鎮軍參軍，寧喪還家。

translations.literal: From Censor of the Southern Secretariat he became Military Adviser to Wang Jingwen, General of the Garrison; after completing mourning he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: From censor of the Southern Secretariat he became military adviser to Wang Jingwen, General of the Garrison; after completing mourning for his parent he returned home.

sentences.zh: 元徽初，桂陽王休範在尋陽，以巨源有筆翰，遣船迎之，餉以錢物。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanhui era, Prince Guiyang Liu Xiufan was at Xunyang; because Juyuan had literary talent, he sent a boat to welcome him and presented him with money and goods.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yuanhui era, Prince Guiyang Liu Xiufan was at Xunyang. Because Juyuan had literary talent, the prince sent a boat to welcome him and presented him with money and goods.

sentences.zh: 巨源因太祖自啓，敕板起巨源使留京都。

translations.literal: Juyuan thereupon petitioned the Founding Emperor himself; an edict was issued appointing Juyuan and ordering him to remain in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Juyuan thereupon petitioned the Founding Emperor directly; an edict was issued appointing him and ordering him to remain in the capital.

sentences.zh: 桂陽事起，使於中書省撰符檄，事平，除奉朝請。

translations.literal: When the Guiyang affair broke out, he was assigned to draft proclamations and summons at the Secretariat; when the matter was settled, he was appointed Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Guiyang rebellion broke out, he was assigned to draft proclamations and summons at the Secretariat. When the affair was settled, he was appointed palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 巨源望有封賞，旣而不獲，乃與尚書令袁粲書曰：

translations.literal: Juyuan hoped for enfeoffment and reward, but in the end received none; thereupon he wrote to Yuan Can, Director of the Secretariat, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Juyuan hoped for enfeoffment and reward, but in the end received none. Thereupon he wrote to Yuan Can, Director of the Secretariat, saying:

sentences.zh: :　　民信理推心，闇於量事，庶謂丹誠感達，賞報孱期；

translations.literal: :　　I, trusting in reason, open my heart; dim in measuring affairs, I hoped my sincere devotion would reach and reward would come soon;
translations.idiomatic: :　　I, trusting in reason, speak from the heart. Though poor at judging affairs, I hoped my sincere devotion would be felt and reward would come soon;

sentences.zh: 豈虞寂寥，忽焉三稔？

translations.literal: who expected solitude—suddenly three years have passed?
translations.idiomatic: who expected to be left in silence while three years suddenly passed?

sentences.zh: 議者必云筆記賤伎，非殺活所待；

translations.literal: Critics will surely say that note-taking is a low craft, not what life and death depend on;
translations.idiomatic: Critics will surely say that note-taking is a low craft, not what matters of life and death depend on;

sentences.zh: 開勸小說，非否判所寄。

translations.literal: composing persuasive pamphlets is not what judgment and decision rely on.
translations.idiomatic: and that composing persuasive pamphlets is not what judgment and decision rely on.

sentences.zh: 然則先聲後實，軍國舊章，七德九功，將名當世。

translations.literal: Yet first sound then substance is the old rule of army and state; the seven virtues and nine accomplishments will make one's name in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Yet first sound and then substance is the old rule of army and state, and the seven virtues and nine accomplishments are what make one's name in an age.

sentences.zh: 仰觀天緯，則右將而左相，俯察人序，則西武而東文，固非胥祝之倫伍，巫匠之流匹矣。

translations.literal: Looking up at celestial patterns, the Right General is on the right and the Chancellor on the left; looking down at human order, martial west and literary east—clearly not the class of scribes and diviners, shamans and craftsmen.
translations.idiomatic: Looking up at the patterns of heaven, the Right General stands on the right and the Chancellor on the left; looking down at human order, martial worthies stand in the west and literary men in the east. This is clearly not the class of scribes and diviners, shamans and craftsmen.

sentences.zh: :　　去昔奇兵，變起呼吸，雖凶渠卽勦，而人情更迷。

translations.literal: :　　In the past the elite troops were deployed; change arose in a breath; though the chief rebel was immediately suppressed, popular sentiment grew more confused.
translations.idiomatic: :　　When elite troops were deployed in the past, crisis arose in a breath. Though the chief rebel was quickly suppressed, popular sentiment grew only more confused.

sentences.zh: 茅恬開城，千齡出叛，當此之時，心膂胡、越，奉迎新亭者，士庶填路，投名朱雀者，愚智空閨，人惑而民不惑，人畏而民不畏，其一可論也。

translations.literal: Mao Tian opened the city gates; Qian Ling went out in rebellion. At that time, with heart and backbone from Hu and Yue, those welcoming at Xinting filled the roads with gentry and commoners; those submitting names at Zhuque emptied homes of fool and sage alike. Others were confused, but I was not; others feared, but I did not—the first point may be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Tian opened the city gates and Qian Ling went out in rebellion. At that time, with heart and backbone from Hu and Yue, those welcoming the rebels at Xinting filled the roads with gentry and commoners, and those submitting their names at Zhuque emptied homes of wise and simple alike. Others were confused, but I was not; others feared, but I did not—the first point may be discussed.

sentences.zh: :　　臨機新亭，獨能抽刃斬賊者，唯有張敬兒；

translations.literal: :　　At the critical moment at Xinting, the only one who could draw his blade and slay the rebel was Zhang Jinger;
translations.idiomatic: :　　At the critical moment at Xinting, the only one who could draw his blade and slay the rebel was Zhang Jinger;

sentences.zh: 而中書省獨能奮筆弗顧者，唯有丘巨源。

translations.literal: and of those in the Secretariat who alone could wield the brush without looking back, there was only Qiu Juyuan.
translations.idiomatic: and of those in the Secretariat who alone could wield the brush without hesitation, there was only Qiu Juyuan.

sentences.zh: 文武相方，誠有優劣，就其死亡以決成敗，當崩天之敵，抗不測之禍，請問海內，此膽何如？

translations.literal: Martial and literary compared, there are indeed superior and inferior; judged by facing death to decide success or failure, confronting an enemy that could shake heaven, resisting unforeseen disaster— I ask within the seas, how is this courage?
translations.idiomatic: Compared, martial and literary merit do differ in degree, but judged by facing death to decide success or failure, confronting a heaven-shaking enemy and resisting unforeseen disaster—I ask the realm, how does such courage rank?

sentences.zh: 其二可論也。

translations.literal: The second point may be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: The second point may be discussed.

sentences.zh: :　　又爾時顛沛，普喚文士，黃門中書，靡不畢集，摛翰振藻，非爲乏人，朝廷洪筆，何故假手凡賤？

translations.literal: :　　Moreover, in that turmoil literary men were summoned everywhere; Yellow Gate and Secretariat all gathered without exception; wielding brush and polishing phrases— it was not for lack of people. Why did the court's grand pens borrow hands from common and base men?
translations.idiomatic: :　　Moreover, in that turmoil literary men were summoned everywhere; the Yellow Gate and Secretariat all gathered without exception. There was no lack of men wielding brush and polishing phrases—so why did the court's grand pens borrow hands from common and base men?

sentences.zh: 若以此賊彊盛，勝負難測，羣賢怯不染豪者，則民宜以勇獲賞；

translations.literal: If because these rebels were strong and victory or defeat hard to foretell, the worthy were timid and unstained by boldness, then I ought to be rewarded for courage;
translations.idiomatic: If the rebels were strong and victory or defeat hard to foretell, and the worthy were timid and unstained by boldness, then I ought to be rewarded for courage;

sentences.zh: 若云羽檄之難，必須筆傑，羣賢推能見委者，則民宜以才賜列，其三可論也。

translations.literal: if it is said that proclamations are difficult and require literary genius, and the worthy were chosen by ability and entrusted, then I ought to be granted rank for talent—the third point may be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: if it is said that proclamations are difficult and require literary genius, and the worthy were chosen by ability and entrusted with the task, then I ought to be granted rank for talent—the third point may be discussed.

sentences.zh: :　　竊見桂陽賊賞不赦之條凡二十五人，而李恒、鍾爽同在此例，戰敗後出，罪竝釋然，而吳邁遠族誅之。

translations.literal: :　　I have seen among the Guiyang rebels' unpardonable list twenty-five persons in all; Li Heng and Zhong Shuang were in the same category, came out after defeat, and their crimes were all pardoned— yet Wu Maiyuan's entire clan was executed.
translations.idiomatic: :　　I have seen that among the Guiyang rebels' unpardonable list there were twenty-five persons in all. Li Heng and Zhong Shuang were in the same category; they came forward after defeat and their crimes were all pardoned—yet Wu Maiyuan's entire clan was executed.

sentences.zh: 罰則操筆大禍而操戈尤害，論以賞科，則武人超越而文人埋沒，其四可論也。

translations.literal: In punishment, wielding the brush brought great disaster while wielding the spear was even more harmful; speaking of reward by statute, martial men surpassed while literary men were buried—the fourth point may be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: In punishment, wielding the brush brought great disaster while wielding the spear was treated as even worse; speaking of rewards by statute, martial men were elevated while literary men were buried—the fourth point may be discussed.

sentences.zh: :　　且邁遠置辭，無乃侵慢，民作符檄，肆言詈辱，放筆出手，卽就兖粉。

translations.literal: :　　Moreover, Maiyuan's wording was perhaps merely insolent; I wrote the proclamation, freely cursing and insulting—as soon as the brush left my hand, I would immediately have been ground to powder.
translations.idiomatic: :　　Moreover, Maiyuan's wording was perhaps merely insolent. I wrote the proclamation, freely cursing and insulting—as soon as my brush left my hand, I would immediately have been ground to powder.

sentences.zh: 若使桂陽得志，民若不轘裂軍門，則應腰斬都市，嬰孩脯膾，伊可熟念，其五可論也。

translations.literal: If Guiyang had succeeded, if I were not torn apart at the army gate, then I should have been executed at the waist in the marketplace; infants minced into paste— this may well be pondered deeply; the fifth point may be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: If Guiyang had succeeded, I would either have been torn apart at the army gate or executed in the marketplace; infants minced into paste—this may well be pondered deeply. The fifth point may be discussed.

sentences.zh: :　　往年戎旅，萬有餘甲，十分之中，九分冗隷，可謂衆矣。

translations.literal: :　　In the military campaign of previous years there were more than ten thousand armored men; of ten parts, nine were superfluous attendants— one may say they were many.
translations.idiomatic: :　　In last year's military campaign there were more than ten thousand armored men; nine-tenths of them were superfluous attendants—one may say the ranks were full.

sentences.zh: 攀龍附驎，翻焉雲翔。

translations.literal: Clinging to dragons and attaching to unicorns, they soared like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Clinging to dragons and attaching to unicorns, they soared like clouds.

sentences.zh: 至若民狂夫，可謂寡矣。

translations.literal: As for me, a reckless fellow, one may say I was few.
translations.idiomatic: As for me, a reckless fellow, one may say I stood alone.

sentences.zh: 徒關敕旨，空然泥沈。

translations.literal: Only concerned with the imperial edict, vainly stuck in mud and sunk.
translations.idiomatic: I cared only for the imperial edict and threw myself in vain into the mire.

sentences.zh: 詎其荷瞂塵末，皆是白起，操牘事始，必非魯連邪？

translations.literal: How could it be that those bearing shields in the dusty rear are all Bai Qi, and those who wielded documents at the outset were certainly not Lu Lian?
translations.idiomatic: How could it be that every soldier bearing a shield in the dusty rear is treated as Bai Qi, yet those who wielded the brush at the outset were surely no Lu Lian?

sentences.zh: 民傎，國算迅足，馳烽旆之機，帝擇逸翰，赴羅之會。

translations.literal: I threw myself into peril; the nation's reckoning moved swiftly; I raced toward the moment of beacon fires and banners; the Emperor selected my skilled brush to meet the gathering where nets were laid.
translations.idiomatic: I threw myself into peril. The nation's reckoning moved swiftly; I raced toward the moment of beacon fires and banners; the Emperor selected my skilled brush to meet the perilous crisis.

sentences.zh: 旣能陵敵不殿，爭先無負，宜其微賜存在，少沾飲齕。

translations.literal: Since I could press the enemy without falling behind and strive to be first without falling short, there ought to have been some small reward, a little share of sustenance.
translations.idiomatic: Since I could press the enemy without falling behind and strive to be first without falling short, there ought to have been some small reward, a little share of sustenance.

sentences.zh: 遂乃棄之溝間，如蜉如蟻，擲之言外，如土如灰。

translations.literal: Yet I was cast aside in the ditch like mayflies and ants, thrown outside discourse like dirt and ash.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I was cast aside in the ditch like mayflies and ants, thrown outside the realm of discourse like dirt and ash.

sentences.zh: 絓隷帖戰，無拳無勇，竝隨資峻級矣；

translations.literal: Hanger-on soldiers attached to battle, without strength or courage, all rose through high ranks according to seniority;
translations.idiomatic: Hanger-on soldiers who tagged along in battle, without strength or courage, all rose through high ranks according to seniority;

sentences.zh: 凡豫臺內，不文不武，已坐拱清階矣。

translations.literal: All those within the Secretariat who were neither literary nor martial already sat on the high clear steps.
translations.idiomatic: All those within the Secretariat who were neither literary nor martial already sat on the high clear steps.

sentences.zh: 撫骸如此，瞻例如彼，旣非草木，何能弭聲？

translations.literal: Touching my bones like this, looking at the example like that— since I am not grass or wood, how can I suppress my voice?
translations.idiomatic: When I touch my own bones and look at the example set by others, since I am not grass or wood, how can I keep silent?

sentences.zh: 巨源竟不被申。

translations.literal: Juyuan in the end was not granted a hearing.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Juyuan's petition was not granted.

sentences.zh: 歷佐諸王府，轉羽林監。

translations.literal: He successively served various princely households and was transferred to Supervisor of the Feathered Forest Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served various princely households and was transferred to supervisor of the Feathered Forest Guard.

sentences.zh: 建元元年，爲尚書主客郎，領軍司馬，越騎校尉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan he served as Gentleman of the Ministry of Receptions, Army Marshal of the Garrison Command, and Colonel of the Yue Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianyuan he served as Gentleman of the Ministry of Receptions, army marshal of the Garrison Command, and colonel of the Yue Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 除武昌太守，拜竟，不樂江外行，世祖問之，巨源曰：「古人云：『寧飲建業水，不食武昌魚。』

translations.literal: He was appointed Administrator of Wuchang; when the appointment was announced, he was unhappy about serving outside the Yangzi region. The Emperor asked him, and Juyuan said: "The ancients said: 'Better to drink the water of Jianye than eat the fish of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed administrator of Wuchang. When the appointment was announced, he was unhappy about serving west of the Yangzi. When the Emperor asked him, Juyuan said, "The ancients said, 'Better to drink the water of Jianye than eat the fish of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 臣年已老，寧死於建業。」

translations.literal: Your subject is already old; better to die in Jianye."
translations.idiomatic: I am already old and would rather die in Jianye."

sentences.zh: 以爲餘杭令。

translations.literal: He was appointed Magistrate of Yuhang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Yuhang instead.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之事，太祖使巨源爲尚書符荊州，巨源以此又望賞異，自此意常不滿。

translations.literal: During the affair of Shen Youzhi, the Founding Emperor had Juyuan draft the Secretariat dispatch to Jingzhou; Juyuan again hoped for special reward for this, and from then on was often discontent.
translations.idiomatic: During the affair of Shen Youzhi, the Founding Emperor had Juyuan draft the Secretariat dispatch to Jingzhou. Juyuan again hoped for special reward for this, and from then on was often discontent.

sentences.zh: 高宗爲吳興，巨源作《秋胡詩》，有譏刺語，以事見殺。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao was in Wuxing, Juyuan composed the Poem on Qiuhu with satirical language; because of the affair he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao was in Wuxing, Juyuan composed the Poem on Qiuhu with satirical language. Because of the affair he was executed.

sentences.zh: 王智深

translations.literal: Wang Zhisen
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhisen

sentences.zh: 王智深字雲才，琅邪臨沂人也。

translations.literal: Wang Zhisen, courtesy name Yuncai, was a native of Linyi in Langya.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhisen, courtesy name Yuncai, was from Linyi in Langya commandery.

sentences.zh: 少從陳郡謝超宗學屬文。

translations.literal: In youth he studied literary composition under Xie Chaozong of Chen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he studied literary composition under Xie Chaozong of Chen commandery.

sentences.zh: 好飲酒，拙澀乏風儀。

translations.literal: He loved drinking wine; he was clumsy, awkward, and lacking in bearing.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine, but was clumsy, awkward, and lacking in bearing.

sentences.zh: 宋建平王景素爲南徐州，作《觀法篇》，智深和之，見賞，辟爲西曹書佐。

translations.literal: When Prince Jianping Liu Jingsu of Song was in Southern Xuzhou, he composed the "Observing the Law" chapter; Zhisen harmonized with it, was appreciated, and was recruited as Western Bureau Secretary Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jianping Liu Jingsu of Song served as governor of Southern Xuzhou, he composed the Observing the Law chapter. Zhisen harmonized with it, won praise, and was recruited as secretary assistant in the Western Bureau.

sentences.zh: 貧無衣，未到職而景素敗。

translations.literal: Poor and without clothes, he had not yet taken up his post when Jingsu was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Too poor to afford clothes, he had not yet taken up his post when Jingsu was defeated.

sentences.zh: 後解褐爲州祭酒。

translations.literal: Later he entered service and was appointed Chancellor of the Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later he entered official service and was appointed chancellor of the province.

sentences.zh: 太祖爲鎮軍時，丘巨源薦之於太祖，板爲府行參軍，除豫章王國常侍，遷太學博士，豫章王大司馬參軍，兼記室。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor was General of the Garrison, Qiu Juyuan recommended him to the Founding Emperor; he was appointed Staff Officer of the headquarters, appointed Attendant of the Principality of Yuzhang, promoted to Erudite of the Imperial University, Military Adviser to the Grand Marshal of Yuzhang, and concurrently Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor was General of the Garrison, Qiu Juyuan recommended him to the Founding Emperor. He was appointed staff officer of the headquarters, attendant of the Principality of Yuzhang, erudite of the Imperial University, military adviser to the Grand Marshal of Yuzhang, and concurrently recorder.

sentences.zh: 世祖使太子家令沈約撰《宋書》，擬立《袁粲傳》，以審世祖。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Crown Prince Household Steward Shen Yue to compile the Book of Song and proposed establishing a Biography of Yuan Can to test the Emperor's reaction.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Crown Prince Household Steward Shen Yue to compile the Book of Song and proposed establishing a biography of Yuan Can to test the Emperor's reaction.

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「袁粲自是宋家忠臣。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Yuan Can was naturally a loyal minister of the Song house."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Yuan Can was naturally a loyal minister of the Song house."

sentences.zh: 約又多載孝武、明帝諸鄙瀆事，上遣左右謂約曰：「孝武事迹不容頓爾。

translations.literal: Yue also included many vulgar and disrespectful matters concerning Xiaowu and Mingdi; the Emperor sent attendants to tell Yue: "The deeds of Xiaowu cannot be dismissed so abruptly.
translations.idiomatic: Yue also included many vulgar and disrespectful matters concerning Xiaowu and Mingdi. The Emperor sent attendants to tell Yue, "The deeds of Xiaowu cannot be dismissed so abruptly.

sentences.zh: 我昔經事宋明帝，卿可思諱惡之義。」

translations.literal: I once served under Emperor Song Mingdi; you should consider the meaning of concealing evil."
translations.idiomatic: I once served under Emperor Ming of Song; you should consider the meaning of concealing evil."

sentences.zh: 於是多所省除。

translations.literal: Thereupon much was cut and removed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon much was cut and removed.

sentences.zh: 又敕智深撰《宋紀》，召見芙蓉堂，賜衣服，給宅。

translations.literal: He also ordered Zhisen to compile the Annals of Song, summoned him to Furong Hall, bestowed clothing, and granted a residence.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Zhisen to compile the Annals of Song, summoned him to Furong Hall, bestowed clothing on him, and granted him a residence.

sentences.zh: 智深告貧於豫章王，王曰：「須卿書成，當相論以祿。」

translations.literal: Zhisen reported his poverty to the Prince of Yuzhang; the Prince said: "When your book is finished, I shall discuss salary with you."
translations.idiomatic: Zhisen reported his poverty to the Prince of Yuzhang. The prince said, "When your book is finished, I shall discuss salary with you."

sentences.zh: 書成三十卷，世祖後召見智深於璿明殿，令拜表奏上。

translations.literal: When the book was finished in thirty volumes, the Emperor later summoned Zhisen to Xuanming Hall and ordered him to submit a memorial presenting it.
translations.idiomatic: When the book was finished in thirty volumes, the Emperor later summoned Zhisen to Xuanming Hall and ordered him to submit a memorial presenting it.

sentences.zh: 表未奏而世祖崩。

translations.literal: Before the memorial was submitted, the Emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: Before the memorial was submitted, the Emperor died.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，敕索其書，智深遷爲竟陵王司徒參軍，坐事免。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longchang an edict demanded the book; Zhisen was transferred to Military Adviser to the Prince of Jingling, Grand Minister of Education, and was dismissed because of an affair.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longchang an edict demanded the book. Zhisen was transferred to military adviser to the Prince of Jingling, Grand Minister of Education, and was dismissed because of an affair.

sentences.zh: 江夏王鋒衡陽王鈞竝善待之。

translations.literal: Prince Jiangxia Liu Feng and Prince Hengyang Liu Jun both treated him well.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jiangxia Liu Feng and Prince Hengyang Liu Jun both treated him well.

sentences.zh: 初，智深爲司徒袁粲所接，及撰宋紀，意常依依。

translations.literal: At first Zhisen was taken in by Grand Minister Yuan Can; when he compiled the Annals of Song, his feelings were always attached.
translations.idiomatic: At first Zhisen was taken in by Grand Minister Yuan Can, and when he compiled the Annals of Song his feelings remained deeply attached.

sentences.zh: 粲幼孤，祖母名其爲愍孫，後慕荀粲，自改名，會稽賀喬譏之，智深於是著論。

translations.literal: Yuan Can was orphaned in youth; his grandmother named him Minsun; later admiring Xun Can, he changed his own name; He Qiao of Kuaiji mocked this, and Zhisen thereupon wrote a treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Can was orphaned in youth, and his grandmother named him Minsun. Later, admiring Xun Can, he changed his own name. He Qiao of Kuaiji mocked this, and Zhisen thereupon wrote a treatise.

sentences.zh: 家貧無人事，嘗餓五日不得食，掘莧根食之。

translations.literal: His family was poor and without visitors; once he went hungry for five days without food and dug amaranth roots to eat.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor and he had few visitors. Once he went hungry for five days without food and dug amaranth roots to eat.

sentences.zh: 司空王僧虔及子志分其衣食。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Wang Sengqian and his son Zhi shared their food and clothing with him.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Wang Sengqian and his son Zhi shared their food and clothing with him.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 先是陳郡袁炳，字叔明，有文學，亦爲袁粲所知。

translations.literal: Before this, Yuan Bing of Chen Commandery, styled Shuming, possessed literary learning and was also known to Yuan Can.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier there had been Yuan Bing of Chen Commandery, courtesy name Shuming, a man of letters who had also won the esteem of Yuan Can.

sentences.zh: 著《晉書》未成，卒。

translations.literal: He authored a History of Jin but it was not completed when he died.
translations.idiomatic: He began a History of Jin but died before finishing it.

sentences.zh: 潁川庾銑，善屬文，見賞豫章王，引至大司馬記室參軍，卒。

translations.literal: Yu Rui of Yingchuan was skilled at literary composition, was appreciated by the Prince of Yuzhang, was brought in as Recorder-Adjutant of the Grand Marshal, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Rui of Yingchuan excelled at prose. The Prince of Yuzhang took notice of him and appointed him recorder-adjutant on the Grand Marshal's staff; he died in office.

sentences.zh: 陸厥

translations.literal: Lu Jue
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jue

sentences.zh: 陸厥字韓卿，吳郡吳人，揚州別駕閑子也。

translations.literal: Lu Jue, styled Hanqing, was a native of Wu in Wu Commandery and was the son of Xian, Assistant Governor of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jue, courtesy name Hanqing, was a native of Wu in Wu Commandery and the son of Xian, deputy governor of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 厥少有風概，好屬文，五言詩體甚新變。

translations.literal: Jue in youth had presence of spirit, loved literary composition, and his five-character verse style was greatly innovative.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Lu Jue had force of character and loved to write. His five-character poetry was strikingly fresh and innovative.

sentences.zh: 永明九年，詔百官舉士，同郡司徒左西掾顧暠之表薦焉。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yongming, an edict ordered all officials to recommend scholars; Gu Hao-zhi, Left Western Attendant of the Minister of Works and a man of the same commandery, memorialized recommending him.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yongming (491), the throne ordered officials to recommend worthy men; Gu Hao-zhi of the same commandery, left western attendant on the Minister of Works' staff, submitted a memorial recommending him.

sentences.zh: 州舉秀才，王晏少傅主簿，遷後軍行參軍。

translations.literal: The province recommended him as a cultivated talent; he served as chief clerk to Wang Yan, Junior Mentor, and was transferred to Acting Adjutant of the Rear Army.
translations.idiomatic: The province nominated him as a cultivated talent. He served as chief clerk to the Junior Mentor Wang Yan, then was promoted to acting adjutant on the rear army staff.

sentences.zh: 永明末，盛爲文章。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongming, he flourished in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years of the Yongming era he became one of the period's leading writers.

sentences.zh: 吳興沈約、陳郡謝朓、琅邪王融以氣類相推轂。

translations.literal: Shen Yue of Wuxing, Xie Tiao of Chen Commandery, and Wang Rong of Langya promoted one another as kindred spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yue of Wuxing, Xie Tiao of Chen Commandery, and Wang Rong of Langya championed one another as literary kindred spirits.

sentences.zh: 汝南周顒善識聲韻。

translations.literal: Zhou Yong of Runan was skilled at recognizing tones and rhyme.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yong of Runan had a fine ear for tones and rhyme.

sentences.zh: 約等文皆用宮商，以平上去入爲四聲，以此制韻，不可增減，世呼爲「永明體」。

translations.literal: The writings of Yue and the others all used gong and shang tones; taking level, rising, departing, and entering as the four tones, they regulated rhyme by this method—it could not be increased or reduced—and the age called it the Yongming style.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yue and his circle wrote with tonal modulation—level, rising, departing, and entering as the four tones—and composed rhyme by fixed rules that admitted no addition or subtraction. The age came to call this the Yongming style.

sentences.zh: 沈約《宋書謝靈運傳》後又論宮商。

translations.literal: After Shen Yue's Biography of Xie Lingyun in the History of Song, he again discussed gong and shang.
translations.idiomatic: In his biography of Xie Lingyun in the History of Song, Shen Yue had already gone on to discuss tonal modulation.

sentences.zh: 厥與約書曰：

translations.literal: Jue wrote to Yue saying:
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jue wrote to Shen Yue:

sentences.zh: :　　范詹事《自序》「性別宮商，識清濁，特能適輕重，濟艱難。

translations.literal: Director Fan's Self-Preface states: By nature I distinguish gong from shang and know clear from muddy tones; I am especially able to suit light and heavy and to rescue difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: In his Self-Preface, Director Fan wrote: By nature I distinguish gong from shang and discern clear from muddy tones; I am especially able to balance weight and lightness and to smooth out what is hard.

sentences.zh: 古今文人，多不全了斯處，縱有會此者，不必從根本中來。」

translations.literal: Writers ancient and modern for the most part do not fully understand this point; even those who occasionally grasp it need not have arrived at it from the root.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient and modern writers have for the most part not fully mastered this point; even those who sometimes hit upon it have not necessarily arrived at it from first principles.

sentences.zh: 沈尚書亦云「自靈均以來，此祕未睹」。

translations.literal: Minister Shen also said: Since Ling Jun, this secret has not been seen.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Shen likewise wrote that since Qu Yuan's day this secret has gone unseen.

sentences.zh: 或「闇與理合，匪由思至。

translations.literal: Or: Darkly in accord with reason, not reached by thought.
translations.idiomatic: Or again: It accords with reason in ways one cannot see, not by deliberate thought alone.

sentences.zh: 張蔡曹王，曾無先覺，潘陸顏謝，去之彌遠」。

translations.literal: Zhang, Cai, Cao, and Wang never had foreknowledge; Pan, Lu, Yan, and Xie grew ever more distant from it.
translations.idiomatic: Among Zhang Heng, Cai Yong, Cao Zhi, and Wang Can there was never a pioneer in this art; among Pan Yue, Lu Ji, Yan Yanzhi, and Xie Lingyun the distance only grew.

sentences.zh: 大旨鈞使「宮羽相變，低昂舛節。

translations.literal: The main gist makes one say: Gong and yu alternate; low and high clash in rhythm.
translations.idiomatic: The main thrust of your doctrine states: Gong and yu tones alternate; highs and lows must not fall out of step.

sentences.zh: 若前有浮聲，則後須切響，一簡之內，音韻盡殊，兩句之中，輕重悉異」。

translations.literal: If the first has a floating tone, then the latter must have a sharp echo; within one line all sounds and rhymes are distinct; within two lines all light and heavy are different.
translations.idiomatic: If the first half carries a lighter tone, the second must answer with a sharper one; within a single line every syllable must differ in sound and rhyme, and across two lines light and heavy must be wholly distinct.

sentences.zh: 辭旣美矣，理又善焉。

translations.literal: The wording is already beautiful, and the reasoning is also good.
translations.idiomatic: The language is elegant and the reasoning sound.

sentences.zh: 但觀歷代衆賢，似不都闇此處，而云「此祕未睹」，近於誣乎？

translations.literal: But observing worthy men of successive ages, they seem not all to have been ignorant of this point—yet to say this secret has not been seen comes close to falsehood, does it not?
translations.idiomatic: Yet when one looks at the great writers of past ages, they do not all seem wholly ignorant of this art—so to say this secret has gone unseen comes close to slander, does it not?

sentences.zh: :　　案范云「不從根本中來」。

translations.literal: Examining Fan's words not from the root:
translations.idiomatic: Regarding Fan's claim that mastery does not come from first principles:

sentences.zh: 尚書云「匪由思至」。

translations.literal: The Minister said not reached by thought.
translations.idiomatic: the Minister writes that it is not reached by deliberate thought.

sentences.zh: 斯可謂揣情謬於玄黃，擿句差其音律也。

translations.literal: This may be called reading sentiment wrongly in black and yellow, or picking out lines that miss their tonal pattern.
translations.idiomatic: This is like misreading intent in what is black and white, or singling out lines that miss their proper tonal pattern.

sentences.zh: 范又云「時有會此者」。

translations.literal: Fan also said there are times when one grasps this.
translations.idiomatic: Fan also admits that there are times when one hits upon it.

sentences.zh: 尚書云「或闇與理合」。

translations.literal: The Minister said sometimes darkly in accord with reason.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister writes that it sometimes accords with reason in ways one cannot see.

sentences.zh: 則美詠清謳，有辭章調韻者，雖有差謬，亦有會合，推此以往，可得而言。

translations.literal: Then fine song and clear ode, writings with regulated diction and rhyme—even if there are errors, there are also matches; extending this onward, one may speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: Beautiful lyrics and polished verse—works with patterned diction and rhyme—may err here and there yet still contain passages that fit; extend the principle and the case can be stated plainly.

sentences.zh: 夫思有合離，前哲同所不免，文有開塞，卽事不得無之。

translations.literal: Thought has union and separation—former sages alike cannot avoid this; writing has openness and blockage—given the matter, it cannot be without these.
translations.idiomatic: Thought has its moments of clarity and confusion, which no sage entirely escapes; writing has its fluent and obstructed passages, which no author can wholly avoid.

sentences.zh: 子建所以好人譏彈，士衡所以遺恨終篇。

translations.literal: This is why Zijian was subject to others' ridicule and censure, and why Shiheng left regret at the end of his pieces.
translations.idiomatic: This is why Cao Zhi invited others' ridicule, and why Lu Ji ended his works with acknowledged regret.

sentences.zh: 旣曰遺恨，非盡美之作，理可詆訶。

translations.literal: Since it is called remaining regret, it is not a work of complete beauty, and it is reasonable that it could be criticized.
translations.idiomatic: If a work is said to carry remaining regret, it is not perfection itself, and criticism is only fair.

sentences.zh: 君子執其詆訶，便謂合理爲闇。

translations.literal: The gentleman seizes on the criticism and then takes what accorded with reason to be ignorance.
translations.idiomatic: The critic seizes on such faults and treats passages that do fit the rule as if they were born of ignorance.

sentences.zh: 豈如指其合理而寄詆訶爲遺恨邪？

translations.literal: How is it like pointing at what accorded with reason and making the criticism into remaining regret?
translations.idiomatic: Should one not rather acknowledge what fits the rule and treat the censure as the source of remaining regret?

sentences.zh: :　　自魏文屬論，深以清濁爲言，劉楨奏書，大明體勢之致，岨峿妥怗之談，操末續顛之說，興玄黃於律呂，比五色之相宣，苟此祕未睹，茲論爲何所指邪？

translations.literal: From Emperor Wen of Wei's treatises, deeply taking clear and muddy as their theme, through Liu Zhen's memorial clearly setting forth the qualities of form and force, talks of steep peaks and smooth levels, theories of broken endings and linked inversions—raising dark and yellow within pitch-pipes, comparing the mutual display of five colors—if this secret has not been seen, to what do these discussions point?
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Wen of Wei's essays, with their emphasis on clear versus muddy tones, to Liu Zhen's memorial expounding form and force, treatises on rugged and smooth style, and theories of broken endings and linked inversions—setting pitch-pipes against the interplay of the five colors—if this secret truly went unseen, what were all these earlier critics talking about?

sentences.zh: 故愚謂前英已早識宮徵，但未屈曲指的，若今論所申。

translations.literal: Therefore this dull one considers that former worthies early knew gong and zhi, but only did not bend and point it out as clearly as the present discourse sets forth.
translations.idiomatic: I take it that earlier masters already grasped gong and zhi tones long ago—they simply did not spell out the point with the precision of your present thesis.

sentences.zh: 至於掩瑕藏疾，合少謬多，則臨淄所云「人之著述，不能無病」者也。

translations.literal: As for hiding flaws and concealing faults, having fewer hits and more errors—this is what the Prince of Linzi meant when he said in human writings there cannot be no flaws.
translations.idiomatic: As for glossing over flaws and keeping faults hidden—more misses than hits—this is exactly what the Prince of Linzi meant by saying that no human writing is without blemish.

sentences.zh: 非知之而不改，謂不改則不知，斯曹、陸又稱「竭情多悔，不可力彊」者也。

translations.literal: It is not that knowing yet not revising—saying not revising means not knowing—this is what Cao and Lu also called exhausting feeling brings much regret; one cannot force strength.
translations.idiomatic: It is not that they knew yet refused to revise; to say that failure to revise means ignorance is to miss what Cao Zhi and Lu Ji meant by to pour out every feeling is to invite much regret—this cannot be forced.

sentences.zh: 今許以有病有悔爲言，則必自知無悔無病之地，引其不了不合爲闇，何獨誣其一合一了之明乎？

translations.literal: Now granting that there are flaws and regrets in speech, one must know there are places without regret or flaw—yet citing what does not fit or is incomplete as ignorance, why only slander their clarity in what fits and is complete?
translations.idiomatic: If one admits flaws and regret in writing, one must also know there are passages without flaw or regret—so to treat what fails or misfits as proof of ignorance while ignoring what succeeds is to slander their clear hits alone.

sentences.zh: 意者亦質文時異，古今好殊，將急在情物，而緩於章句。

translations.literal: Perhaps substance and ornament differ by age, ancient and modern tastes diverge—they will be urgent about feeling and things, and lax about clauses and lines.
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps substance and ornament shift with the age, and tastes change from era to era—earlier writers cared chiefly for emotion and subject matter, and gave less urgency to line and clause.

sentences.zh: 情物，文之所急，美惡猶且相半；

translations.literal: Feeling and things are what writing urgently seeks; good and bad are still half and half;
translations.idiomatic: Emotion and subject matter are what writing most urgently pursues, and even there good and bad run about even;

sentences.zh: 章句，意之所緩，故合少而謬多。

translations.literal: Clauses and lines are what intent treats lightly, therefore fewer hits and more errors.
translations.idiomatic: line and clause were what they treated lightly, and so hits were fewer and misses more numerous.

sentences.zh: 義兼於斯，必非不知明矣。

translations.literal: The meaning encompasses this; it surely is not ignorance that is clear.
translations.idiomatic: When both points are taken together, it can hardly be ignorance that is at issue.

sentences.zh: :　　《長門》、《上林》，殆非一家之賦，《洛神》、《池鴈》，便成二體之作。

translations.literal: Changmen and Shanglin are scarcely the work of one house; Luoshen and Chiyan straightaway become writings of two styles.
translations.idiomatic: The Changmen Rhapsody and the Shanglin Rhapsody can hardly be called the work of a single hand; the Luoshen Rhapsody and the Goose Pond Rhapsody plainly belong to two different styles.

sentences.zh: 孟堅精正，詠史無虧於東主，平子恢富，《羽獵》不累於憑虛。

translations.literal: Mengjian was refined and upright—his Ode on History did not fall short of the Eastern Lord's; Pingzi was vast and rich—Feathered Hunt did not weigh down Upon Emptiness.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu was precise and upright—his Ode on History does not suffer beside the Eastern Lord's work; Zhang Heng was expansive and rich—his Feathered Hunt does not drag down his Upon Emptiness.

sentences.zh: 王粲《初征》，他文未能稱是；

translations.literal: Wang Can's First Campaign—his other writings could not be called the same;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Can's First Campaign stands apart—his other pieces cannot be called its equal;

sentences.zh: 楊脩敏捷，《暑賦》彌日不獻。

translations.literal: Yang Xiu was quick—Summer Heat Rhapsody went a whole day without being presented.
