translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiu was quick-witted, yet his Summer Heat Rhapsody took a full day and still was not finished.

sentences.zh: 率意寡尤，則事促乎一日；

translations.literal: Following intent with few faults, then the affair is rushed within one day;
translations.idiomatic: when one follows the flow and errs little, the work may be done in a day;

sentences.zh: 翳翳愈伏，而理賒於七步。

translations.literal: Gradually more subdued, yet the reasoning extends to seven paces.
translations.idiomatic: when inspiration dims and the mind grows sluggish, the argument may stretch to seven paces.

sentences.zh: 一人之思，遲速天懸；

translations.literal: One person's thought—slow and fast are heaven's span apart;
translations.idiomatic: Within a single mind, speed and slowness may be worlds apart;

sentences.zh: 一家之文，工拙壤隔。

translations.literal: One family's writings—skill and clumsiness are separated by earth's breadth.
translations.idiomatic: within a single author's corpus, mastery and mediocrity may stand as far apart as heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 何獨宮商律呂，必責其如一邪？

translations.literal: Why only gong, shang, pitch-pipes, and scales—must one demand they be uniform?
translations.idiomatic: Why should gong, shang, pitch-pipes, and scales alone be held to perfect uniformity?

sentences.zh: 論者乃可言未窮其致，不得言曾無先覺也。

translations.literal: The disputant may say its reach is not fully exhausted, but may not say there was never foreknowledge.
translations.idiomatic: One may say the doctrine has not yet been fully exhausted, but one may not say there was never any foreknowledge at all.

sentences.zh: 約答曰：

translations.literal: Yue replied saying:
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yue replied:

sentences.zh: :　　宮商之聲有五，文字之別累萬，以累萬之繁，配五聲之約，高下低昂，非思力所舉。

translations.literal: The sounds of gong and shang are five, while the distinctions among written characters accumulate to tens of thousands; with tens of thousands of complexity to match the constraint of five tones, high, low, and pitch are not what mental force can accomplish.
translations.idiomatic: There are five notes in the gong-shang scale, yet written characters number in the tens of thousands. To match that vast complexity to the narrow compass of five tones—balancing high, low, and pitch—is beyond what deliberate thought can achieve.

sentences.zh: 又非止若斯而已也。

translations.literal: And it is not only like this and nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: And the difficulty does not stop there.

sentences.zh: 十字之文，顛倒相配，字不過十，巧歷已不能盡，何況復過於此者乎？

translations.literal: A text of ten characters, matched in inverted pairs—with no more than ten characters, even a skilled reckoner cannot exhaust the combinations; how much less when there are more than this?
translations.idiomatic: In a passage of ten characters, permuted and paired, there are no more than ten glyphs—yet even a master calculator could not exhaust the combinations. How much more so when the text runs longer?

sentences.zh: 靈均以來，未經用之於懷抱，固無從得其髣彿矣。

translations.literal: Since Ling Jun, it has not been applied in the breast, so there is naturally no way to obtain even a likeness of it.
translations.idiomatic: Since Qu Yuan's day no one has truly applied this art in composition, and so there is no way even to glimpse its likeness.

sentences.zh: 若斯之妙，而聖人不尚，何邪？

translations.literal: If its subtlety is like this, yet the sages did not esteem it—why?
translations.idiomatic: If the art is so subtle, why did the sages not prize it?

sentences.zh: 此蓋曲折聲韻之巧，無當於訓義，非聖哲立言之所急也。

translations.literal: This is probably the craft of winding tones and rhyme—irrelevant to instructive meaning, not what the sage and wise urgently set forth in speech.
translations.idiomatic: This is merely the clever manipulation of winding tones and rhyme. It has nothing to do with moral instruction, and was never what the sages urgently sought in their teaching.

sentences.zh: 是以子雲譬之「雕蟲篆刻」，云「壯夫不爲」。

translations.literal: Therefore Ziyun compared it to carved insects and seal-script engraving, saying a strong man does not do this.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Yang Xiong likened it to ornamental insect carving and seal-script engraving, saying that a grown man does not stoop to such work.

sentences.zh: :　　自古辭人，豈不知宮羽之殊，商征之別。

translations.literal: Since antiquity, have writers not known the difference between gong and yu, and between shang and zhi?
translations.idiomatic: Writers since antiquity surely knew the difference between gong and yu, and between shang and zhi.

sentences.zh: 雖知五音之異，而其中參差變動，所昧實多，故鄙意所謂「此祕未睹」者也。

translations.literal: Although they knew the differences among the five tones, the uneven variations within them were much that remained obscure—this is what my humble opinion calls this secret has not been seen.
translations.idiomatic: They knew the five tones differed, but the uneven shifts within them remained largely obscure—this is what I mean by saying this secret has gone unseen.

sentences.zh: 以此而推，則知前世文士便未悟此處。

translations.literal: Extending from this, one knows that writers of former ages simply had not awakened to this point.
translations.idiomatic: Extend the logic and it follows that earlier writers had not truly grasped this point.

sentences.zh: :　　若以文章之音韻，同弦管之聲曲，則美惡妍蚩，不得頓相乖反。

translations.literal: If the tones and rhyme of literary composition were the same as the melodies of string and pipe, then beauty and ugliness, grace and coarseness, could not suddenly oppose one another.
translations.idiomatic: If the tonal pattern of a literary work were the same as the melody of string and pipe, then beauty and ugliness, grace and coarseness, could not suddenly contradict one another.

sentences.zh: 譬由子野操曲，安得忽有闡緩失調之聲，以《洛神》比陳思他賦，有似異手之作。

translations.literal: It is like when Ziye plays a tune—how could there suddenly be a broad, slack, out-of-tune sound? Comparing the Luoshen Rhapsody with Lord Chensi's other rhapsodies, it seems the work of a different hand.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Kuang played a tune, how could a sudden broad, slack, out-of-key passage appear? Compare the Luoshen Rhapsody with Cao Zhi's other rhapsodies—it reads like the work of another hand.

sentences.zh: 故知天機啓，則律呂自調；

translations.literal: Therefore one knows that when heavenly inspiration opens, pitch-pipes tune themselves;
translations.idiomatic: This shows that when inspiration flows freely, pitch and tone fall into place of themselves;

sentences.zh: 六情滯，則音律頓舛也。

translations.literal: When the six emotions stagnate, then tones and rhythm suddenly go wrong.
translations.idiomatic: when the six emotions stall, rhythm and tone at once go awry.

sentences.zh: :　　士衡雖云「炳若縟錦」，寧有濯色江波，其中復有一片是衞文之服？

translations.literal: Although Shiheng said bright as brocaded silk, could there be cloth dyed in river waves, with within it again a piece that is the robe of Duke Wen of Wei?
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji may have said that a work shines like brocade—but could brocade washed in river water contain within it a patch of Duke Wen of Wei's robe?

sentences.zh: 此則陸生之言，卽復不盡者矣。

translations.literal: This then is what Master Lu said, and even so it is not exhaustive.
translations.idiomatic: Even Lu Ji's remark, apt as it is, does not say everything.

sentences.zh: 韻與不韻，復有精麤，輪扁不能言，老夫亦不盡辨此。

translations.literal: Rhyme and non-rhyme again have fine and coarse degrees; Lun Bian could not speak of it, and this old man also does not fully distinguish this.
translations.idiomatic: Whether a passage rhymes or not admits degrees of refinement and coarseness. Lun Bian could not put the craft into words, and I too cannot fully sort out every case.

sentences.zh: 永元元年，始安王遙光反，厥父閑被誅，厥坐繫尚方，尋有赦令，厥恨父不及，感慟而卒，年二十八。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongyuan, the Prince of Shian Yao Guang rebelled; Jue's father Xian was executed; Jue was imprisoned in the Palace Workshops; soon there was an amnesty edict; Jue grieved that his father did not reach it, was moved to anguish and died, aged twenty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongyuan (499), when the Prince of Shian, Xiao Yaoguang, rebelled, Lu Jue's father Xian was executed. Lu Jue was imprisoned in the Palace Workshops. An amnesty soon followed, but he grieved that his father had not lived to see it, and died of grief at the age of twenty-eight.

sentences.zh: 文集行於世。

translations.literal: His collected writings circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 會稽虞炎，永明中以文學與沈約俱爲文惠太子所遇，意眄殊常。

translations.literal: Yu Yan of Kuaiji, during Yongming for literary learning together with Shen Yue was favored by Crown Prince Wen Hui, whose regard was exceptionally uncommon.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yan of Kuaiji, noted for his learning during the Yongming era, was favored along with Shen Yue by Crown Prince Wen Hui, who regarded him with unusual warmth.

sentences.zh: 官至驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: He reached office as General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the rank of General of Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 崔慰祖

translations.literal: Cui Weizu
translations.idiomatic: Cui Weizu

sentences.zh: 崔慰祖字悅宗，清河東武城人也。

translations.literal: Cui Weizu, styled Yuezong, was a native of Dongwucheng in Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Weizu, courtesy name Yuezong, was a native of Dongwucheng in Qinghe Commandery.

sentences.zh: 父慶緒，永明中，爲梁州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Qingxu, during Yongming, served as Governor of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qingxu served as governor of Liang Province during the Yongming era.

sentences.zh: 慰祖解褐奉朝請。

translations.literal: Weizu upon leaving office sackcloth entered service as Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: Weizu began his career as an attendant at court.

sentences.zh: 父喪不食鹽，母曰：「汝旣無兄弟，又未有子胤。

translations.literal: During his father's mourning he ate no salt; his mother said: You have no brothers and still have no son and heir.
translations.idiomatic: During his father's mourning he abstained from salt. His mother said: You have no brothers and still no son to carry on the line.

sentences.zh: 毀不滅性，政當不進肴羞耳，如何絕鹽！

translations.literal: Self-mortification does not extinguish one's nature—you should merely not take savory dishes, so how can you cut off salt entirely!
translations.idiomatic: Grief must not destroy your life. You need only forgo rich foods—not cut off salt altogether!

sentences.zh: 吾今亦不食矣。」

translations.literal: I too will not eat now.
translations.idiomatic: If you will not eat, then I shall not eat either.

sentences.zh: 慰祖不得已從之。

translations.literal: Weizu had no choice but to follow her.
translations.idiomatic: Weizu had no choice but to comply.

sentences.zh: 父梁州之資，家財千萬，散與宗族，漆器題爲日字，日字之器，流乎遠近。

translations.literal: His father's assets from Liang Province—family wealth of ten million—he distributed to the clan; lacquerware was inscribed with the character for sun, and sun-marked vessels circulated near and far.
translations.idiomatic: His father's wealth from Liang Province amounted to ten million cash. He distributed it among his clan, marking lacquerware with the character ri (sun); vessels so marked spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 料得父時假貰文疏，謂族子紘曰：「彼有，自當見還；

translations.literal: Having obtained the loan documents from his father's time, he said to his clansman Hong: If they have the means, they will naturally return what is owed;
translations.idiomatic: When he came upon his father's loan records, he told his clansman Hong: Those who have the means will repay in their own time;

sentences.zh: 彼無，吾何言哉！」

translations.literal: If they do not, what can I say!
translations.idiomatic: those who do not—what more is there to say?

sentences.zh: 悉火焚之。

translations.literal: He burned them all in the fire.
translations.idiomatic: He burned them all.

sentences.zh: 好學，聚書至萬卷，隣里年少好事者來從假借，日數十袠，慰祖親自取與，未常爲辭。

translations.literal: He loved learning and gathered books to ten thousand scrolls; young neighbors fond of such things came to borrow from him, dozens of fascicles daily; Weizu personally took and gave them out and never made excuse.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and amassed a library of ten thousand scrolls. Young neighbors who shared his interests came to borrow books—dozens of fascicles a day—and Weizu personally fetched and returned them, never refusing.

sentences.zh: 爲始安王撫軍墨曹行參軍，轉刑獄，兼記室。

translations.literal: He served as Acting Adjutant of the Ink Office on the Prince of Shian's Pacification Army staff, was transferred to Criminal Cases, and concurrently served as Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting adjutant in the ink office on the Prince of Shian's pacification army staff, then moved to criminal cases and concurrently served as recorder.

sentences.zh: 遙光好棋，數召慰祖對戲，慰祖輙辭拙，非朔望不見也。

translations.literal: Yaoguang loved weiqi and repeatedly summoned Weizu to play against him; Weizu always pleaded clumsiness and would not appear except on the first and fifteenth of the month.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoguang loved weiqi and often summoned Weizu to play, but Weizu always pleaded incompetence and would see him only on the first and fifteenth of the month.

sentences.zh: 建武中，詔舉士，從兄慧景舉慰祖及平原劉孝標，竝碩學。

translations.literal: During Jianwu, an edict recommended scholars; his cousin Huijing recommended Weizu and Liu Xiaobiao of Pingyuan, both great scholars.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianwu era, when the throne ordered officials to recommend scholars, his cousin Huijing nominated Weizu and Liu Xiaobiao of Pingyuan, both noted for deep learning.

sentences.zh: 帝欲試以百里，慰祖辭不就。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to test him with a hundred-li district; Weizu declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to test him with a district magistracy, but Weizu declined.

sentences.zh: 國子祭酒沈約、吏部郎謝朓嘗於吏部省中賔友俱集，各問慰祖地理中所不悉十餘事，慰祖口吃，無華辭，而酬據精悉，一座稱服之。

translations.literal: Director of the National University Shen Yue and Department Director Xie Tiao once gathered with guests and friends in the Department of Personnel office; each asked Weizu more than ten things in geography that they did not understand; Weizu stuttered and had no flowery rhetoric, yet answered with precise mastery of evidence, and the whole assembly praised and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the National University Shen Yue and Department Director Xie Tiao once gathered with friends in the personnel office and each put more than a dozen geographical questions to Weizu on points they did not know. Weizu stuttered and had no polished rhetoric, yet answered with precise command of the sources, and the whole company was impressed.

sentences.zh: 朓歎曰：「假使班、馬復生，無以過此。」

translations.literal: Tiao sighed and said: Even if Ban and Sima were reborn, they could not surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Tiao sighed and said: Even if Ban Gu and Sima Qian were alive again, they could not do better.

sentences.zh: 慰祖賣宅四十五萬，買者云：「寧有減不？」

translations.literal: Weizu sold his house for four hundred fifty thousand; the buyer said: Can there be a reduction?
translations.idiomatic: Weizu sold his house for four hundred fifty thousand cash. The buyer asked: Could you come down on the price?

sentences.zh: 答曰：「誠慚韓伯休，何容二價。」

translations.literal: He replied: I am truly ashamed before Han Boxiu—how could there be two prices?
translations.idiomatic: He replied: I would be ashamed before Han Kang—how could I name two prices?

sentences.zh: 買者又曰：「君但責四十六萬，一萬見與。」

translations.literal: The buyer again said: Sir, simply charge four hundred sixty thousand—I will give you the extra ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The buyer said again: Just ask four hundred sixty thousand—I will give you the extra ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 慰祖曰：「是卽同君欺人，豈是我心乎？」

translations.literal: Weizu said: That would be the same as you deceiving people—how could that be my intent?
translations.idiomatic: Weizu said: That would mean joining you in cheating others—is that what I intend?

sentences.zh: 少與侍中江祀款，及祀貴，常來候之，而慰祖不往也。

translations.literal: In youth he was close with Attendant-in-Ordinary Jiang Si; when Si became eminent, he often came to visit him, but Weizu did not go to him.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was on close terms with Attendant-in-Ordinary Jiang Si. When Si rose high, he often came to call on Weizu, but Weizu never returned the visits.

sentences.zh: 與丹陽丞劉渢素善，遙光據東府反，慰祖在城內。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with Liu Hong, Assistant Magistrate of Danyang; Yaoguang held the Eastern Palace and rebelled, and Weizu was inside the city.
translations.idiomatic: He was also close to Liu Hong, assistant magistrate of Danyang. When Yaoguang seized the Eastern Palace and rebelled, Weizu was inside the city walls.

sentences.zh: 城未潰一日，渢謂之曰：「卿有老母，宜其出矣。」

translations.literal: One day before the city was breached, Hong said to him: "You have an aged mother—you should leave the city."
translations.idiomatic: One day before the city fell, Hong told him, "You have an old mother at home—you ought to get out while you can."

sentences.zh: 命門者出之。

translations.literal: He ordered the gatekeepers to let him out.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the gatekeepers to let him pass out of the city.

sentences.zh: 慰祖詣闕自首。

translations.literal: Weizu went to the palace gate and surrendered himself.
translations.idiomatic: Weizu presented himself at the imperial court to confess his guilt.

sentences.zh: 繫尚方，病卒。

translations.literal: He was imprisoned in the Directorate of Imperial Manufactories and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was held in the Directorate of Imperial Manufactories, where he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 慰祖著《海岱志》，起太公迄西晉人物，爲四十卷，半未成。

translations.literal: Weizu wrote the Record of Hai and Dai, covering figures from the Grand Duke through the Western Jin in forty volumes, half of which were unfinished.
translations.idiomatic: Weizu authored the Record of Hai and Dai, treating figures from the Grand Duke of Qi through the Western Jin in forty juan, of which only half were completed.

sentences.zh: 臨卒，與從弟緯書云：「常欲更注遷、固二史，採史、漢所漏二百餘事，在廚簏，可檢寫之，以存大意。

translations.literal: Near death he wrote to his younger cousin Wei, saying: "I always wanted to revise the annotations to the histories of Sima Qian and Ban Gu, collecting over two hundred matters omitted from the Records and the History of Han, kept in the kitchen cabinet—you may look them out and copy them to preserve the main points.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he wrote his younger cousin Wei: "I had long wished to revise the commentaries on Sima Qian and Ban Gu, gathering more than two hundred items the Records and the History of Han had overlooked; they are in the kitchen cabinet. You may find them, copy them out, and keep the substance.

sentences.zh: 《海岱志》良未周悉，可寫數本，付護軍諸從事人一通，及友人任昉、徐夤、劉洋、裴揆。」

translations.literal: The Record of Hai and Dai is still far from thorough—a few copies may be made, one copy given to the Protector Army clerks, and also to friends Ren Fang, Xu Yin, Liu Yang, and Pei Kui."
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Hai and Dai is still far from complete. Make several copies: one for the clerks of the Protector Army, and others for my friends Ren Fang, Xu Yin, Liu Yang, and Pei Kui."

sentences.zh: 又令「以棺親土，不須塼，勿設靈座」。

translations.literal: He also directed: "Let the coffin touch the earth directly—no need for brick, and do not set up a spirit seat."
translations.idiomatic: He also instructed: "Let the coffin rest directly on the earth—no brick lining, and no spirit seat."

sentences.zh: 時年三十五。

translations.literal: He was thirty-five years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was thirty-five at the time.

sentences.zh: 王逡之

translations.literal: Wang Qunzhi
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qunzhi

sentences.zh: 王逡之字宣約，琅邪臨沂人也。

translations.literal: Wang Qunzhi, courtesy name Xuanyue, was a native of Linyi in Langya.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qunzhi, courtesy name Xuanyue, was from Linyi in Langya commandery.

sentences.zh: 父祖皆爲郡守。

translations.literal: His father and grandfather both served as grand administrators of commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Both his father and grandfather had served as provincial grand administrators.

sentences.zh: 逡之少禮學博聞。

translations.literal: In youth Qunzhi was steeped in ritual learning and broad in his erudition.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Qunzhi was steeped in ritual studies and widely read.

sentences.zh: 起家江夏王國常侍，大司馬行參軍，章安令，累至始安內史。

translations.literal: He began his career as Attendant of the Principality of Jiangxia, Staff Officer to the Grand Marshal, Magistrate of Zhang'an, and rose in succession to Interior Minister of Shi'an.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as attendant of the Principality of Jiangxia, staff officer to the Grand Marshal, and magistrate of Zhang'an, rising in time to interior minister of Shi'an.

sentences.zh: 不之官，除山陽王驃騎參軍，兼治書御史，安成國郎中，吳令。

translations.literal: He did not take up his post; he was appointed Military Adviser to the Valiant Cavalry of the Prince of Shanyang, and concurrently Drafting Secretary, Gentleman of the Principality of Ancheng, and Magistrate of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He declined to take up one appointment and was instead appointed military adviser to the Prince of Shanyang's Valiant Cavalry, with concurrent posts as drafting secretary, gentleman of the Principality of Ancheng, and magistrate of Wu.

sentences.zh: 昇明末，右僕射王儉重儒術，逡之以著作郎兼尚書左丞，參定齊國儀禮。

translations.literal: At the end of the Shengming era, Right Vice Director Wang Jian valued Confucian learning; Qunzhi was made Editor and concurrently Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat, to help fix the ritual code of the state of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Shengming era, Right Vice Director Wang Jian valued Confucian learning. Qunzhi was appointed editor and concurrently Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat to help codify Qi ritual.

sentences.zh: 初，儉撰《古今喪服集記》，逡之難儉十一條。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jian compiled the Comprehensive Record of Mourning Garments Ancient and Modern, and Qunzhi raised eleven objections to Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jian had compiled the Comprehensive Record of Mourning Garments Ancient and Modern; Qunzhi challenged him on eleven points.

sentences.zh: 更撰《世行》五卷。

translations.literal: He rewrote the Conduct of the Ages in five volumes.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote the Conduct of the Ages in five juan.

sentences.zh: 轉國子博士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 國學久廢，建元二年，逡之先上表立學，又兼著作，撰《永明起居注》。

translations.literal: The imperial academy had long fallen into disuse; in the second year of Jianyuan, Qunzhi was first to memorialize to establish the school; he also concurrently served as editor and compiled the Yongming Daily Records.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial academy had long lain abandoned. In the second year of Jianyuan, Qunzhi was the first to memorialize for its revival; he also served concurrently as editor and compiled the Yongming Daily Records.

sentences.zh: 轉通直常侍，驍騎將軍，領博士、著作如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Direct Regular Attendant, Valiant Cavalry General, continuing to head the erudite and editorial posts as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Direct Regular Attendant and Valiant Cavalry General, retaining his posts as erudite and editor.

sentences.zh: 出爲寧朔將軍、南康相，太中、光祿大夫，加侍中。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as General of Pacifying the North and Administrator of Nankang, Grand Master of Palace Counsel, and Chamberlain for Attendants, with additional appointment as Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as General of Pacifying the North and administrator of Nankang, then promoted to Grand Master of Palace Counsel and Chamberlain for Attendants, with the additional title of Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 逡之率素，衣裘不澣，机案塵黑，年老，手不釋卷。

translations.literal: Qunzhi was plain and unadorned—his fur robes unwashed, his desk and case black with dust; though aged, he never put down his scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Qunzhi lived plainly: his fur robes went unwashed, his desk and writing case were black with dust, and even in old age he never set his scrolls aside.

sentences.zh: 建武二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Jianwu.

sentences.zh: 從弟珪之，有史學，撰《齊職儀》。

translations.literal: His younger cousin Guizhi had skill in historical studies and compiled the Qi Official Protocol.
translations.idiomatic: His younger cousin Guizhi was skilled in historical studies and compiled the Qi Official Protocol.

sentences.zh: 永明九年，其子中軍參軍顥上啓曰：「臣亡父故長水校尉珪之，藉素爲基，依儒習性。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yongming, his son Hao, a military adviser to the Central Army, submitted a memorial saying: "My late father, the former Colonel of the Long River Guizhi, took plain integrity as his foundation and relied on Confucian training for his nature.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yongming, his son Hao, a staff officer of the Central Army, submitted a memorial: "My late father, the former Colonel of the Long River Guizhi, made plain integrity his foundation and shaped his character through Confucian study.

sentences.zh: 以宋元徽二年，被敕使纂集古設官歷代分職，凡在墳策，必盡詳究。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanhui of Song, by imperial order he was charged to compile the ancient establishment of offices and the division of duties through the ages; whatever lay in archive records, he examined exhaustively.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanhui under the Song, by imperial command he was tasked with compiling the history of government offices and their division of duties through the ages, investigating every record preserved in the archives.

sentences.zh: 是以等級掌司，咸加編錄。

translations.literal: Thus every grade and office was entered in full.
translations.idiomatic: Every rank and office was therefore fully recorded.

sentences.zh: 黜陟遷補，悉該研記。

translations.literal: Dismissals, promotions, transfers, and replacements were all traced and noted.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissals, promotions, transfers, and replacements were all traced and annotated.

sentences.zh: 述章服之差，兼冠佩之飾。

translations.literal: He set forth the distinctions of robes and insignia, and also caps and girdle ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: He treated distinctions in robes and insignia together with caps and girdle ornaments.

sentences.zh: 屬值啓運，軌度惟新。

translations.literal: It happened that a new dynasty was arising and standards were being reshaped.
translations.idiomatic: This came just as the dynasty was being founded anew and its institutions were being remade.

sentences.zh: 故太宰臣淵奉宣敕旨，使速洗正。

translations.literal: The late Grand Preceptor, Minister Yuan, received and proclaimed the imperial command, ordering a prompt revision and correction.
translations.idiomatic: The late Grand Preceptor Xiao Yuan received and proclaimed the imperial command that the work be swiftly revised and corrected.

sentences.zh: 刊定未畢，臣私門凶禍。

translations.literal: The editorial work was not finished when calamity struck my private household.
translations.idiomatic: Revision was not yet complete when disaster struck my family.

sentences.zh: 不揆庸微，謹冒啓上，凡五十卷，謂之《齊職儀》。

translations.literal: Without measuring my own meagerness, I respectfully venture this submission—altogether fifty volumes, entitled the Qi Official Protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Underestimating my own meagerness, I respectfully submit this work—all fifty juan, entitled the Qi Official Protocol.

sentences.zh: 仰希永升天閣，長銘祕府。」

translations.literal: I look up in hope that it may forever ascend to the Heavenly Pavilion and be long preserved in the Secret Repository.
translations.idiomatic: I earnestly hope it may be received into the Imperial Archives and long preserved in the Secret Repository.

sentences.zh: 詔付祕閣。

translations.literal: An edict ordered it deposited in the Secret Repository.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the work deposited in the Secret Repository.

sentences.zh: 祖沖之

translations.literal: Zu Chongzhi
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi

sentences.zh: 祖沖之字文遠，范陽薊人也。

translations.literal: Zu Chongzhi, courtesy name Wenyuan, was a native of Ji in Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi, courtesy name Wenyuan, was from Ji in Fanyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖昌，宋大匠卿。

translations.literal: Zu Chang served as Master of Works in the Song.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chang had served as Master of Works under the Song.

sentences.zh: 父朔之，奉朝請。

translations.literal: His father Shuozhi was an Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shuozhi held the rank of Attendant at Court.

sentences.zh: 沖之少稽古，有機思。

translations.literal: In youth Chongzhi investigated antiquity and had an ingenious turn of mind.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Chongzhi steeped himself in antiquity and possessed a keenly inventive mind.

sentences.zh: 宋孝武使直華林學省，賜宅宇車服。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of Song had him serve directly in the Hualin Academicians' Office and granted him a residence and carriage and robes.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu of Song had him serve directly in the Hualin Academicians' Office and granted him a residence, carriage, and formal robes.

sentences.zh: 解褐徐州迎從事，公府參軍。

translations.literal: Upon first appointment he served as Assistant for Reception in Xuzhou and Staff Officer of a princely headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Upon entering office he served as reception assistant in Xuzhou and staff officer at a princely headquarters.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉中，用何承天所制歷，比古十一家爲密，沖之以爲尚疏，乃更造新法。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era of Song they used the calendar He Chengtian had devised, which was more precise than the eleven ancient schools; Chongzhi thought it still too loose and therefore devised a new method.
translations.idiomatic: During Song Yuanjia the court used the calendar He Chengtian had devised, tighter than the eleven ancient systems; Chongzhi still found it too loose and devised a new method.

sentences.zh: 上表曰：

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: :　　臣博訪前墳，遠稽昔典，五帝𨇠次，三王交分，《春秋》朔氣，《紀年》薄蝕，談、遷載述，彪、固列志，魏世注歷，晉代《起居》，探異今古，觀要華戎。

translations.literal: ": Your servant has broadly consulted the old tomes and traced the ancient canons: the sequence of the Five Emperors, the alternating divisions of the Three Dynasties; the new moon and qi in the Spring and Autumn Annals, eclipses in the Bamboo Annals; accounts by Tan and Qian, treatises by Biao and Gu, the annotated calendars of Wei, and the Daily Records of Jin—I have sought what differs between past and present and gathered the essentials for China and the frontier."
translations.idiomatic: ": I have consulted the ancient records and traced the old canon—from the ordered reigns of the Five Emperors and the successive divisions of the Three Dynasties to the new-moon qi in the Spring and Autumn Annals and the eclipses in the Bamboo Annals; from the chronicles of Tan and Sima Qian and the treatises of Biao and Ban Gu to Wei's annotated calendars and Jin's Daily Records. I have weighed past against present and gathered what is essential for the Central Lands and the frontier."

sentences.zh: 書契以降，二千餘稔，日月離會之徵，星度疏密之驗。

translations.literal: Since the age of writing began, more than two thousand years have passed—the signs of the sun's and moon's conjunctions and separations, the proofs of the stars' sparse and dense placement.
translations.idiomatic: Since the age of written records, more than two thousand years have passed—the signs of solar and lunar conjunction and separation, the tests of stellar positions whether sparse or dense.

sentences.zh: 專功耽思，咸可得而言也。

translations.literal: Those who devoted themselves wholly and brooded deeply—all may be spoken of.
translations.idiomatic: All that specialists have achieved through devoted labor and deep reflection can be set forth.

sentences.zh: 加以親量圭尺，躬察儀漏，目盡毫氂，心窮籌筴，考課推移，又曲備其詳矣。

translations.literal: Added to this, I personally measured the gnomon and rule, personally inspected instruments and clepsydras; my eye exhausted every hair's breadth, my mind exhausted every counting rod; in verifying and assessing change over time, I have once again made the details complete.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, I have measured the gnomon and rule myself, inspected instruments and water clocks myself, examined matters to the finest hair's breadth and calculated them through to the last rod—in testing how things shift over time I have again made every detail complete.

sentences.zh: :　　然而古曆疏舛，類不精密，羣氏糾紛，莫審其會。

translations.literal: ": Yet the ancient calendars were loose and errant, mostly inexact; the many schools disputed one another, and none could discern the true meeting points."
translations.idiomatic: ": Yet the ancient calendars were loose and full of error, broadly imprecise; the many schools argued among themselves, and none could discern the true conjunctions."

sentences.zh: 尋何承天所上，意存改革，而置法簡略，今已乖遠。

translations.literal: When I examine what He Chengtian submitted, his intent was reform, but the methods he set up were abbreviated and simple—today they are already far off.
translations.idiomatic: Examining what He Chengtian submitted, his aim was reform, but the methods he established were abbreviated and simple—and they are already far wide of the mark.

sentences.zh: 以臣校之，三睹厥謬，日月所在，差覺三度，二至晷景，幾失一日，五星見伏，至差四旬，留逆進退，或移兩宿。

translations.literal: When I compare against it, thrice I have seen its errors: the sun and moon's positions differ by nearly three degrees; the solstice gnomon shadows miss by nearly a day; the five planets' appearances and disappearances miss by as much as forty days; their stations, reversals, advances, and retreats sometimes shift by two lodges.
translations.idiomatic: By my reckoning I have thrice seen its errors: the positions of sun and moon are off by nearly three degrees; solstice gnomon shadows miss by nearly a whole day; the five planets' appearances and disappearances are off by as much as forty days; their pauses, reversals, advances, and retreats sometimes shift by two lunar lodges.

sentences.zh: 分至失實，則節閏非正；

translations.literal: When the equinoxes and solstices miss the truth, then intercalary months and seasons are not correct;
translations.idiomatic: when the equinoxes and solstices miss the truth, intercalation and the seasons fall out of alignment;

sentences.zh: 宿度違天，則伺察無准。

translations.literal: when lodge-degrees violate Heaven, then observation and scrutiny have no standard.
translations.idiomatic: when stellar degrees diverge from Heaven, observation has no reliable standard.

sentences.zh: 臣生屬聖辰，詢逮在運，敢率愚瞽，更創新曆。

translations.literal: Your servant was born in a sage age and has reached the turning of fortune; I dare to lead my foolish blindness and create a new calendar anew.
translations.idiomatic: I was born under a sage reign and have lived to see Heaven's turning; led by my own imperfect sight, I dare to create a new calendar.

sentences.zh: :　　謹立改易之意有二，設法之情有三。

translations.literal: ": I respectfully set forth two principles for change and three points in the design of methods."
translations.idiomatic: ": I respectfully set forth two principles for reform and three points in how the method is to be structured."

sentences.zh: 改易者一：以舊法一章，十九歲有七閏，閏數爲多，經二百年輙差一日。

translations.literal: The first change: under the old method one cycle gave seven intercalary months in nineteen years—the number of intercalations was too many, and after two hundred years one day was soon off.
translations.idiomatic: The first reform: under the old method, nineteen years contained seven intercalary months—the number of intercalations was too high, and after two centuries the calendar was soon off by a day.

sentences.zh: 節閏旣移，則應改法，歷紀屢遷，寔由此條。

translations.literal: Once intercalation and seasons shift, the method ought to be changed; calendars have been altered again and again, and this is truly the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Once intercalation and the seasons drift, the method must change—this, in truth, is why calendars have been revised again and again.

sentences.zh: 今改章法三百九十一年有一百四十四閏，令却合周、漢，則將來永用，無復差動。

translations.literal: Now the intercalation rule is changed to one hundred forty-four intercalations in three hundred ninety-one years, making it accord with the Zhou and Han—then hereafter it may be used forever without further error.
translations.idiomatic: The new intercalation rule sets one hundred forty-four intercalations in three hundred ninety-one years, bringing the calendar back into accord with Zhou and Han usage—so that hereafter it may be used indefinitely without further drift.

sentences.zh: 其二：以堯典云「日短星昴，以正仲冬」。

translations.literal: The second: the Canon of Yao says, "The days are short and the star is Mao—thereby fixing midwinter."
translations.idiomatic: The second concerns the Canon of Yao, which says: "The day is short and the star Mao stands at zenith—thereby to fix midwinter."

sentences.zh: 以此推之，唐世冬至日，在今宿之左五十許度。

translations.literal: Extrapolating from this, the winter solstice in the age of Tang lay some fifty or so degrees to the left of its present lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Extrapolating from this, Tang-era winter solstice fell some fifty degrees or so to the west of its present lodge position.

sentences.zh: 漢代之初，卽用秦曆，冬至日在牽牛六度。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han they immediately used the Qin calendar; the winter solstice lay at six degrees within Ox.
translations.idiomatic: At the Han founding the court immediately adopted the Qin calendar, placing winter solstice at six degrees within the Ox lodge.

sentences.zh: 漢武改立《太初曆》，冬至日在牛初。

translations.literal: Han Wudi established the Taichu Calendar anew; the winter solstice lay at the start of Ox.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han established the Taichu Calendar afresh, placing winter solstice at the beginning of the Ox lodge.

sentences.zh: 後漢四分法，冬至日在斗二十二。

translations.literal: The Four-Part method of Later Han placed winter solstice at twenty-two degrees within Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: The Quarter-Remainder Calendar of Later Han placed winter solstice at twenty-two degrees within the Dipper lodge.

sentences.zh: 晉世姜岌以月蝕檢日，知冬至在斗十七。

translations.literal: In Jin times Jiang Kui tested the sun by lunar eclipse and knew winter solstice lay at seventeen in Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin times Jiang Kui tested the sun by lunar eclipse and found winter solstice at seventeen degrees within Dipper.

sentences.zh: 今參以中星，課以蝕望，冬至之日，在斗十一。

translations.literal: Now comparing by the culminating stars and verifying by eclipse and full moon, the day of winter solstice lies at eleven in Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Comparing now by culmination stars and verifying by eclipses and full moons, winter solstice falls at eleven degrees within Dipper.

sentences.zh: 通而計之，未盈百載，所差二度。

translations.literal: Computing it throughout, in less than a full century the deviation is two degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Taken together, in less than a century the deviation amounts to two degrees.

sentences.zh: 舊法竝令冬至日有定處，天數旣差，則七曜宿度，漸與舛訛。

translations.literal: The old methods all fixed winter solstice at one place; once the heavenly numbers had drifted, the seven luminaries' lodge-degrees gradually became mistaken and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Old methods all fixed winter solstice at a single position; once the heavenly cycles drifted, the lodge degrees of the seven luminaries gradually came adrift.

sentences.zh: 乖謬旣著，輙應改易。

translations.literal: Once the error was plain, change ought to follow at once.
translations.idiomatic: Once the error is plain, revision must follow at once.

sentences.zh: 僅合一時，莫能通遠。

translations.literal: They fit only a single age and cannot extend far.
translations.idiomatic: Such fixes suit only a single age and cannot extend far into time.

sentences.zh: 遷革不已，又由此條。

translations.literal: Revisions without end come from this article too.
translations.idiomatic: Endless rounds of revision stem from this same flaw.

sentences.zh: 今令冬至所在歲歲微差，却檢漢注，竝皆審密，將來久用，無煩屢改。

translations.literal: Now winter solstice is made to shift slightly year by year; checked against Han annotations, all are exact—and for long future use there will be no need for repeated changes.
translations.idiomatic: Under the new method winter solstice shifts slightly year by year; checked against Han-era annotations all is exact—and for long use hereafter there will be no need for repeated revisions.

sentences.zh: 又設法者，其一：以子爲辰首，位在正北，爻應初九升氣之端，虛爲北方列宿之中。

translations.literal: As for the design of methods—the first: take zi as head of the branches, its position due north, its line corresponding to the ascending qi at the first nine of the hexagram; Emptiness is the middle of the northern lodges.
translations.idiomatic: As for the design of methods—the first: let zi serve as head of the earthly branches, positioned due north, corresponding to the first nine line where ascending qi begins; the Emptiness lodge marks the center of the northern asterisms.

sentences.zh: 元氣肇初，宜在此次。

translations.literal: At the first emergence of primordial qi, the starting point ought to lie here.
translations.idiomatic: At the first emergence of primordial qi, the starting point ought to lie here.

sentences.zh: 前儒虞喜，備論其義。

translations.literal: The earlier Confucian Yu Xi fully discussed this principle.
translations.idiomatic: The earlier scholar Yu Xi discussed this principle at length.

sentences.zh: 今曆上元日度，發自虛一。

translations.literal: Now the calendar's origin-era solar degree begins from Emptiness one.
translations.idiomatic: In the new calendar the origin-era solar degree begins from the first degree of Emptiness.

sentences.zh: 其二：以日辰之號，甲子爲先，歷法設元，應在此歲。

translations.literal: The second: among the designations of day and branch, jiazi comes first; when a calendar sets its origin, it ought to fall in that year.
translations.idiomatic: The second: among the names of days and branches, jiazi comes first; when a calendar sets its origin, it ought to fall in that year.

sentences.zh: 而黃帝以來，世代所用，凡十一曆，上元之歲，莫值此名。

translations.literal: Yet from the Yellow Emperor on, through the calendars each age has used—eleven calendars in all—not one origin year has matched this name.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from the Yellow Emperor down through every calendar each age has used—eleven in all—not one origin year has borne this designation.

sentences.zh: 今曆上元歲在甲子。

translations.literal: Now the calendar's origin year falls in jiazi.
translations.idiomatic: In the new calendar the origin year falls in jiazi.

sentences.zh: 其三：以上元之歲，歷中衆條，竝應以此爲始。

translations.literal: The third: in the origin year every item in the calendar ought to begin from this point.
translations.idiomatic: The third: in the origin year every item in the calendar ought to begin from this point.

sentences.zh: 而《景初曆》交會遲疾，元首有差。

translations.literal: Yet in the Jingchu Calendar conjunction, fast and slow motion at the origin had discrepancies.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the Jingchu Calendar the lunar conjunction and the motions of fast and slow at the origin carried discrepancies.

sentences.zh: 又承天法，日月五星，各自有元，交會遲疾，亦竝置差，裁得朔氣合而已，條序紛錯，不及古意。

translations.literal: Again in Chengtian's method, sun, moon, and the five planets each had separate origins; conjunction, fast and slow motion also all bore separate discrepancies—barely making new-moon qi align, while the sequence of clauses was tangled and fell short of the ancient intent.
translations.idiomatic: Chengtian's method likewise gave sun, moon, and the five planets each its own origin; conjunction and fast and slow motion were each assigned separate discrepancies—barely forcing new-moon qi to align while leaving the sequence of rules tangled and far from ancient intent.

sentences.zh: 今設法日月五緯交會遲疾，悉以上元歲首爲始，羣流共源，庶無乖誤。

translations.literal: Now the method sets conjunction and the fast and slow motions of sun, moon, and the five planets all to begin from the head of the origin year, all streams from one source—so that hopefully there will be no error.
translations.idiomatic: The new method sets conjunction and the fast and slow motions of sun, moon, and the five planets all to begin from the origin year's head, with every stream from one source, so that error may hopefully be avoided.

sentences.zh: :　　若夫測以定形，據以實效。

translations.literal: ": As for measuring to fix form and relying on it for actual effect."
translations.idiomatic: ": Measure to fix form; rely on that for actual proof."

sentences.zh: 懸象著明，尺表之驗可推；

translations.literal: The suspended images are bright and clear—the test of gnomon and rule may be extrapolated;
translations.idiomatic: the hanging constellations shine bright—gnomon-and-rule tests can be extrapolated from them;

sentences.zh: 動氣幽微，寸管之候不忒。

translations.literal: The stirring qi is subtle—the gauge of the inch-tube is not wrong.
translations.idiomatic: the stirring of qi is subtle—yet the inch-tube's mark does not err.

sentences.zh: 今臣所立，易以取信。

translations.literal: What your servant has established is easy to trust.
translations.idiomatic: What I have established is easy to put to the proof.

sentences.zh: 但綜覈始終，大存緩密，革新變舊，有約有繁。

translations.literal: But examining beginning and end as a whole, it largely preserves both looseness and tightness; in innovating and changing the old, some parts are abbreviated and some elaborate.
translations.idiomatic: Yet taken from beginning to end, it keeps both slackness and tightness in balance; in replacing the old with the new, some parts are abbreviated and some more elaborate.

sentences.zh: 用約之條，理不自懼，用繁之意，顧非謬然。

translations.literal: In the abbreviated articles the logic does not alarm itself; in the elaborate passages the reasoning is by no means absurd.
translations.idiomatic: Where the rules are abbreviated the logic still holds; where they are elaborate the reasoning is by no means absurd.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why so?

sentences.zh: 夫紀閏參差，數各有分，分之爲體，非不細密，臣是用深惜毫釐，以全求妙之准，不辭積累，以成永定之制，非爲思而莫知，悟而弗改也。

translations.literal: Governing intercalation is uneven and the numbers each have their parts; as a structure those parts are not inexact—your servant therefore cherishes every hair's breadth to preserve the standard of seeking perfection, and does not shrink from accumulation to complete a permanently fixed system—not because one reflects yet knows nothing, or understands yet will not change.
translations.idiomatic: Intercalation is uneven and each number has its allotted part; as structural units those parts are not imprecise. That is why I have clung to every hair's breadth to preserve the standard of exactitude, and have not shrunk from accumulated detail to build a permanently fixed system—not from inability to think through the matter, nor from understanding and yet refusing to change.

sentences.zh: 若所上萬一可採，伏願頒宣羣司，賜垂詳究。

translations.literal: If what is submitted is in any part usable, I prostrate myself in hope that it may be promulgated to the many offices and that your Majesty will deign to examine it in detail.
translations.idiomatic: If any part of what I submit may be adopted, I humbly beg that it be promulgated to the relevant offices and that Your Majesty will deign to examine it closely.

sentences.zh: 事奏。

translations.literal: The matter was submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted.

sentences.zh: 孝武令朝士善曆者難之，不能屈。

translations.literal: Xiaowu ordered court scholars skilled in calendars to challenge it, but they could not refute him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu ordered court scholars skilled in calendrical science to challenge it, but none could refute him.

sentences.zh: 會帝崩，不施行。

translations.literal: When the Emperor happened to die, it was not put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then died, and the calendar was never adopted.

sentences.zh: 出爲婁縣令，謁者僕射。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as Magistrate of Lou and Director of Messengers.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as magistrate of Lou and Director of Messengers.

sentences.zh: 初，宋武平關中，得姚興指南車，有外形而無機巧，每行，使人於內轉之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Wu of Song pacified Guanzhong, he obtained Yao Xing's south-pointing carriage—it had outward form but no inner mechanism, and each time it traveled someone inside had to turn it by hand.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Wu of Song pacified Guanzhong he obtained Yao Xing's south-pointing carriage. It had outward form but no inner mechanism; every time it traveled someone inside had to turn it by hand.

sentences.zh: 昇明中，太祖輔政，使沖之追修古法。

translations.literal: In the Shengming era, when the Founding Emperor served as regent, he had Chongzhi restore the ancient method.
translations.idiomatic: During Shengming, while the Founding Emperor served as regent, he had Chongzhi restore the ancient design.

sentences.zh: 沖之改造銅機，圓轉不窮，而司方如一，馬均以來未有也。

translations.literal: Chongzhi reworked a bronze mechanism that turned without end yet kept direction constant—a thing unseen since Ma Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi rebuilt it with a bronze mechanism that revolved endlessly yet kept true direction—something unseen since Ma Jun.

sentences.zh: 時有北人索馭驎者，亦云能造指南車，太祖使與沖之各造，使於樂遊苑對共校試，而頗有差僻，乃毀焚之。

translations.literal: At the time there was a northerner named Suo Yulin who also claimed he could build a south-pointing carriage; the Founding Emperor had him and Chongzhi each build one and had them tested together face to face at Leyou Park—but theirs was somewhat skewed and off, so it was destroyed by fire.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a northerner named Suo Yulin also claimed he could build a south-pointing carriage. The Founding Emperor had him and Chongzhi each build one and face them off for testing at Leyou Park—but Suo's device was noticeably skewed and defective, so it was destroyed by burning.

sentences.zh: 永明中，竟陵王子良好古，沖之造欹器獻之。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era, Prince Ziliang of Jingling loved antiquity; Chongzhi made a tipping vessel and presented it to him.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongming, Prince Ziliang of Jingling was fond of antiquity. Chongzhi crafted a tipping vessel and presented it to him.

sentences.zh: 文惠太子在東宮，見沖之曆法，啓世祖施行，文惠尋薨，事又寢。

translations.literal: While Crown Prince Wen Hui was in the Eastern Palace, he saw Chongzhi's calendar method and memorialized Emperor Wu to put it into practice; Wen Hui soon died and the matter again lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Wen Hui, while in the Eastern Palace, saw Chongzhi's calendar method and memorialized Emperor Wu to adopt it. Wen Hui soon died, and the matter again lapsed.

sentences.zh: 轉長水校尉，領本職。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Colonel Director of Waters and retained his original post.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Colonel Director of Waters, retaining his original post.

sentences.zh: 沖之造《安邊論》，欲開屯田，廣農殖。

translations.literal: Chongzhi wrote "On Securing the Frontier," aiming to open military colonies and expand agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi composed "On Securing the Frontier," seeking to open military colonies and broaden farming.

sentences.zh: 建武中，明帝使沖之巡行四方，興造大業，可以利百姓者，會連有軍事，事竟不行。

translations.literal: During Jianwu, Emperor Ming had Chongzhi tour the four quarters to undertake great works that could benefit the people; successive military campaigns intervened, and in the end nothing was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: During Jianwu, Emperor Ming sent Chongzhi to tour the realm and launch great undertakings that might benefit the people. Continuous warfare intervened, and in the end the plan was never enacted.

sentences.zh: 沖之解鍾律，博塞當時獨絕，莫能對者。

translations.literal: Chongzhi understood bells and pitch pipes; at gambling games he was uniquely unmatched in his day—none could rival him.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi mastered bells and pitch pipes, and at games of chance he stood alone in his age—no one could match him.

sentences.zh: 以諸葛亮有木牛流馬，乃造一器，不因風水，施機自運，不勞人力。

translations.literal: Because Zhuge Liang had had the wooden ox and flowing horse, he built a device that did not rely on wind or water but used mechanisms to move itself, requiring no human labor.
translations.idiomatic: Recalling that Zhuge Liang had devised the wooden ox and flowing horse, he built a contrivance that needed neither wind nor water but moved of itself through applied mechanism, without human toil.

sentences.zh: 又造千里船，於新亭江試之，日行百餘里。

translations.literal: He also built a thousand-li boat and tested it on the Xinting River—it traveled more than a hundred li in a day.
translations.idiomatic: He also built a thousand-li boat and tested it on the Xinting River, where it covered more than a hundred li in a single day.

sentences.zh: 於樂遊苑造水碓磨，世祖親自臨視。

translations.literal: At Leyou Park he built water-powered stamp mills and grinding mills; Emperor Wu personally came to inspect them.
translations.idiomatic: At Leyou Park he constructed water-powered stamp mills and grinding mills, and Emperor Wu came in person to inspect them.

sentences.zh: 又特善算。

translations.literal: He was also especially skilled at calculation.
translations.idiomatic: He was also exceptionally skilled at calculation.

sentences.zh: 永元二年，沖之卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongyuan, Chongzhi died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongyuan, Chongzhi died.

sentences.zh: 年七十二。

translations.literal: He was seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He was seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 著《易老莊義釋》、《論語孝經注》，《九章》造《綴述》數十篇。

translations.literal: He authored "Exposition of the Meanings of the Changes, Laozi, and Zhuangzi," "Commentary on the Analects and Classic of Filial Piety," and several dozen chapters of "Appended Treatises" on the Nine Chapters.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote "Exposition of the Meanings of the Changes, Laozi, and Zhuangzi," "Commentary on the Analects and Classic of Filial Piety," and several dozen chapters of "Appended Treatises" to the Nine Chapters.

sentences.zh: 賈淵

translations.literal: Jia Yuan
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yuan

sentences.zh: 賈淵字希鏡，平陽襄陵人也。

translations.literal: Jia Yuan, courtesy name Xijing, was a native of Xiangling in Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yuan, courtesy name Xijing, was from Xiangling in Pingyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖弼之，晉員外郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Bizhi was an acting gentleman of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Bizhi served as an acting gentleman of Jin.

sentences.zh: 父匪之，驃騎參軍。

translations.literal: His father Feizhi was an aide in the Rapid Cavalry command.
translations.idiomatic: His father Feizhi was an aide on the staff of the Rapid Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 世傳譜學。

translations.literal: His family transmitted the study of genealogies for generations.
translations.idiomatic: His family had transmitted genealogical scholarship for generations.

sentences.zh: 孝武世，青州人發古冢，銘云「青州世子，東海女郎」。

translations.literal: During Emperor Xiaowu's reign, a man from Qingzhou opened an ancient tomb; its inscription read "Heir of Qingzhou, Maiden of Donghai."
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Xiaowu, a man from Qingzhou excavated an ancient tomb whose inscription read, "Heir of Qingzhou, Maiden of Donghai."

sentences.zh: 帝問學士鮑照、徐爰、蘇寶生，竝不能悉。

translations.literal: The emperor asked the scholars Bao Zhao, Xu Ai, and Su Baosheng—they could not fully explain it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned the scholars Bao Zhao, Xu Ai, and Su Baosheng, but none could explain it fully.

sentences.zh: 淵對曰：「此是司馬越女，嫁苟晞兒。」

translations.literal: Yuan replied, "This is the daughter of Sima Yue, who married the son of Gou Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan answered, "This is the daughter of Sima Yue, who was given in marriage to the son of Gou Xi.

sentences.zh: 檢訪果然。

translations.literal: On investigation it proved to be so.
translations.idiomatic: When investigators checked, they found it was exactly as he had said.

sentences.zh: 由是見遇。

translations.literal: Thereupon he won favor.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he won imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 敕淵注《郭子》。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yuan to annotate the "Book of Guo."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Yuan to annotate the "Book of Guo."

sentences.zh: 泰始初，辟丹陽郡主簿，奉朝請，太學博士，安成王撫軍行參軍，出爲丹徒令。

translations.literal: At the start of Taishi he was recruited as chief clerk of Danyang commandery, appointed Attendant at Court, Erudite of the Imperial Academy, and acting aide on the staff of the Pacifying Army under the Prince of Ancheng, then sent out as magistrate of Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taishi he was recruited as chief clerk of Danyang commandery, appointed Attendant at Court and Erudite of the Imperial Academy, served as acting aide on the Pacifying Army staff under the Prince of Ancheng, and was then sent out as magistrate of Dantu.

sentences.zh: 昇明中，太祖嘉淵世學，取爲驃騎參軍，武陵王國郎中令，補餘姚令。

translations.literal: During Shengming the Founding Emperor admired Yuan's hereditary scholarship and appointed him aide in the Rapid Cavalry command, Director of the Prince of Wuling's household, and slated him for magistrate of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: During Shengming the Founding Emperor, admiring Yuan's hereditary learning, appointed him aide on the Rapid Cavalry staff, Director of the Prince of Wuling's household, and selected him to serve as magistrate of Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 未行，仍爲義興郡丞。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post he was instead made assistant magistrate of Yixing commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up that post he was instead made assistant magistrate of Yixing commandery.

sentences.zh: 永明初，轉尚書外兵郎，歷大司馬司徒府參軍。

translations.literal: At the start of Yongming he was transferred to External Military Affairs Secretary in the Ministry of Works and served successively as staff member in the Grand Marshal's and Minister over the Masses' offices.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yongming he was transferred to External Military Affairs Secretary in the Ministry of Works and served in turn on the staffs of the Grand Marshal and the Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 竟陵王子良使淵撰見客譜，出爲句容令。

translations.literal: Prince Ziliang of Jingling had Yuan compile a register of visiting guests; he was then sent out as magistrate of Jurong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ziliang of Jingling had Yuan compile a guest-reception genealogy, after which he was sent out as magistrate of Jurong.

sentences.zh: 先是譜學未有名家，淵祖弼之廣集百氏譜記，專心治業。

translations.literal: Before this, genealogical studies had had no leading household; Yuan's grandfather Bizhi broadly collected genealogical records of the hundred clans and devoted himself to the craft.
translations.idiomatic: Previously genealogical scholarship had had no great family name; Yuan's grandfather Bizhi gathered genealogical records from the hundred clans on a wide scale and devoted himself entirely to the work.

sentences.zh: 晉太元中，朝廷給弼之令史書吏，撰定繕寫，藏祕閣及左民曹。

translations.literal: During Jin Taixuan the court supplied Bizhi with clerks and copyists to compile and transcribe the records, which were stored in the Secret Archive and the Left Population Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taixuan era of Jin the court provided Bizhi with clerks and copyists to compile and transcribe the records, which were stored in the Secret Archive and the Left Population Bureau.

sentences.zh: 淵父及淵三世傳學，凡十八州士族譜，合百帙七百餘卷，該究精悉，當世莫比。

translations.literal: Yuan's father and Yuan himself carried the learning through three generations—genealogies of gentry clans from eighteen provinces in all, totaling a hundred fascicles and more than seven hundred scrolls, exhaustive and precise, unmatched in their day.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan's father and Yuan himself transmitted the learning through three generations: genealogies of gentry clans from eighteen provinces, a hundred fascicles and more than seven hundred scrolls in all—thorough, precise, and without peer in their age.

sentences.zh: 永明中，衞軍王儉抄次《百家譜》，與淵參懷撰定。

translations.literal: During Yongming, Guard General Wang Jian abridged the "Hundred Clans Genealogy" with Yuan participating in its compilation and editing.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongming, Guard General Wang Jian abridged the "Hundred Clans Genealogy," with Yuan assisting in its compilation and revision.

sentences.zh: 建武初，淵遷長水校尉。

translations.literal: At the start of Jianwu, Yuan was promoted to Colonel Director of Waters.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianwu, Yuan was promoted to Colonel Director of Waters.

sentences.zh: 荒傖人王泰寶買襲琅邪譜，尚書令王晏以啓高宗，淵坐被收，當極法，子棲長謝罪，稽顙流血，朝廷哀之，免淵罪。

translations.literal: A rustic northerner named Wang Taibao purchased and misappropriated the Langye genealogy; Minister over the Masses Wang Yan memorialized Emperor Gaozong. Yuan was implicated, arrested, and faced capital punishment; his son Qichang pleaded guilty, kowtowed until his forehead bled—the court took pity and pardoned Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: A rustic northerner named Wang Taibao bought and seized the Langye genealogy; Minister over the Masses Wang Yan reported the matter to Emperor Gaozong. Yuan was implicated, arrested, and condemned to the extreme penalty. His son Qichang confessed on his behalf, kowtowing until his forehead bled; the court took pity and pardoned Yuan.

sentences.zh: 數年，始安王遙光板撫軍諮議，不就，仍爲北中郎參軍。

translations.literal: Several years later Prince Yao Guang of Shi'an invited him by placard to serve as army counselor on the Pacifying Army staff, but he did not accept and remained a staff member of the Northern Corps Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later Prince Yao Guang of Shi'an invited him by written placard to serve as army counselor on the Pacifying Army staff, but he declined and remained a staff member under the Northern Corps Commander.

sentences.zh: 中興元年，卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongxing, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongxing, he died.

sentences.zh: 年六十二。

translations.literal: He was sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He was sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 撰《氏族要狀》及《人名書》，竝行於世。

translations.literal: He compiled "Essential Records of Clans" and "Book of Personal Names," both of which circulated in his time.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled "Essential Records of Clans" and "Book of Personal Names," both of which circulated widely in his day.

sentences.zh: 史論

translations.literal: Historical Commentary
translations.idiomatic: Historical Commentary

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：文章者，蓋情性之風標，神明之律呂也。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Writing is the banner of one's inner nature and the pitch-pipe of the spirit.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Literature is the standard of temperament and the tuning-pipe of the divine mind.

sentences.zh: 蘊思含毫，遊心內運，放言落紙，氣韻天成。

translations.literal: Thought gathers, the brush held poised; the mind wanders inward in motion; words released fall upon the page, and tonal resonance arises of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Thought gathers as the brush is held poised; the mind roams inward in its workings; words spill onto the page, and breath and cadence take shape of themselves.

sentences.zh: 莫不稟以生靈，遷乎愛嗜，機見殊門，賞悟紛雜。

translations.literal: All draw upon living spirit and shift with private taste; insight opens through divergent gates, and appreciation becomes tangled and mixed.
translations.idiomatic: All partake of living spirit and move with personal inclination; insight appears by different paths, and judgments of worth grow confused and diverse.

sentences.zh: 若子桓之品藻人才，仲治之區判文體，陸機辨於《文賦》，李充論於《翰林》，張視擿句褒貶，顏延圖寫情興，各任懷抱，共爲權衡。

translations.literal: Cao Pi appraised talent, Wang Can distinguished literary forms, Lu Ji argued in the "Rhapsody on Literature," Li Chong discoursed in the "Forest of Letters," Zhang Shi picked out lines for praise and blame, and Yan Yanzhi mapped emotional stirrings—each following his own bent, together serving as a measure.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi appraised men of talent, Wang Can divided literary forms, Lu Ji reasoned in the "Rhapsody on Literature," Li Chong argued in the "Forest of Letters," Zhang Shi extracted lines for praise and blame, and Yan Yanzhi traced the movements of feeling—each trusting his own mind, together forming a standard.

sentences.zh: 屬文之道，事出神思，感召無象，變化不窮。

translations.literal: The way of literary composition arises from divine thought—it summons response without visible form and transforms without end.
translations.idiomatic: The art of writing proceeds from spirit-thought: it evokes what has no image and changes without limit.

sentences.zh: 俱五聲之音響，而出言異句；

translations.literal: Both alike are sounds of the five tones, yet the words they utter form different lines;
translations.idiomatic: both alike are sounds of the five tones, yet the lines they speak take different forms;

sentences.zh: 等萬物之情狀，而下筆殊形。

translations.literal: Equally the conditions of the ten thousand things, yet the brush traces unlike shapes.
translations.idiomatic: equally the conditions of the ten thousand things, yet what falls from the brush takes unlike forms.

sentences.zh: 吟詠規範，本之雅什，流分條散，各以言區。

translations.literal: The norms of chanting and recitation take the canonical odes as their root; streams branch and scatter, each defined by its own wording.
translations.idiomatic: The standards of song and recitation derive from the canonical odes; currents divide and spread, each marked off by its own language.

sentences.zh: 若陳思《代馬》羣章，王粲《飛鸞》諸製，四言之美，前超後絕。

translations.literal: Such as Cao Zhi's suite "Substitute Horses" and Wang Can's pieces "Flying Luan"—in the beauty of four-character verse, unmatched before and without equal after.
translations.idiomatic: Such as Cao Zhi's suite "Substitute Horses" and Wang Can's compositions "Flying Luan"—in the splendor of four-character verse, they surpassed all before and left none after.

sentences.zh: 少卿離辭，五言才骨，難與爭鶩。

translations.literal: Master Shao's parting words—in five-character verse his talent and bone are hard to rival.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiangru's parting words—in five-character verse his talent and sinew are hard to match in rivalry.

sentences.zh: 桂林湘水，平子之華篇，飛館玉池，魏文之麗篆，七言之作，非此誰先。

translations.literal: "Guilin and Xiang Waters"—Zhang Heng's splendid piece; "Flying Tower and Jade Pool"—Emperor Wen of Wei's elegant composition—in seven-character works, who came before these?
translations.idiomatic: "Guilin and Xiang Waters" is Zhang Heng's splendid piece; "Flying Tower and Jade Pool" is Emperor Wen of Wei's elegant composition—in works of seven characters, who came before these?

sentences.zh: 卿、雲巨麗，升堂冠冕，張、左恢廓，登高不繼，賦貴披陳，未或加矣。

translations.literal: Sima Xiangru and Yang Xiong are grandly ornate—they enter the hall crowned; Zhang Heng and Zuo Si are vast and sweeping—they ascend the heights without successors; for fu that prized unfolding exposition, perhaps none surpassed them.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiangru and Yang Xiong are magnificently ornate, entering the hall in full regalia; Zhang Heng and Zuo Si are broad and expansive, climbing high with none to follow; among fu that valued open unfolding, perhaps none surpassed them.

sentences.zh: 顯宗之述傅毅，簡文之摛彥伯，分言制句，多得頌體。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Han's account of Fu Yi, Emperor Jianwen's treatment of Yan Bo—dividing words and crafting lines, mostly achieving the eulogy form.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Han's narration of Fu Yi and Emperor Jianwen's rendering of Yan Bo—by dividing phrases and shaping lines, they mostly attained the eulogy form.

sentences.zh: 裴頠內侍，元規鳳池，子章以來，章表之選。

translations.literal: Pei Wei at the inner court, Yu Liang at the Phoenix Pool—from Zizhang onward, the choice works among memorials and letters.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Wei in attendance at the inner court, Yu Liang at the Phoenix Pool—from Zizhang onward, the finest among memorials and formal letters.

sentences.zh: 孫綽之碑，嗣伯喈之後，謝莊之誄，起安仁之塵，顏延《楊瓚》，自比《馬督》，以多稱貴，歸莊爲允。

translations.literal: Sun Chuo's stele inscription continues after Cai Yong; Xie Zhuang's dirge raises the dust of Pan Yue; Yan Yanzhi's "Yang Zan" compares itself to "Supervisor Ma"—though praised for its abundance, Xie Zhuang's is the one that truly merits it.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chuo's stele inscription follows in the wake of Cai Yong; Xie Zhuang's dirge stirs the dust left by Pan Yue; Yan Yanzhi's "Yang Zan" sets itself beside "Supervisor Ma"—though the former is praised for its fullness, the latter is the one that truly deserves esteem.

sentences.zh: 王褒《僮約》，束皙《發蒙》，滑稽之流，亦可奇瑋。

translations.literal: Wang Bao's "Bondservant's Contract," Shu Xi's "Awakening the Unlettered"—in the vein of jest, also wonderfully strange.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bao's "Bondservant's Contract" and Shu Xi's "Awakening the Unlettered"—works in the comic vein, also marvelously singular.

sentences.zh: 五言之制，獨秀衆品。

translations.literal: The five-character form stands alone among all genres.
translations.idiomatic: The five-character form stands alone, surpassing all other kinds.

sentences.zh: 習玩爲理，事久則瀆，在乎文章，彌患凡舊。

translations.literal: What becomes habit seems natural; what lasts long grows stale—in writing, the dread is all the more commonplace and worn.
translations.idiomatic: What is practiced until familiar becomes principle; what endures long grows stale—in literature, the danger is all the more that of the ordinary and the old.

sentences.zh: 若無新變，不能代雄。

translations.literal: Without fresh innovation, none can replace the old masters.
translations.idiomatic: Without new transformation, none can stand in for the old champions.

sentences.zh: 建安一體，典論短長互出；

translations.literal: The Jian'an school as one style—in "Discourses on Literature" strengths and flaws alternate;
translations.idiomatic: the Jian'an school as one style—in "Discourses on Literature" strengths and flaws appear in turn;

sentences.zh: 潘、陸齊名，機、岳之文永異。

translations.literal: Pan and Lu share equal fame, yet Lu Ji's and Yue's writings remain forever unlike.
translations.idiomatic: Pan and Lu share equal renown, yet the writings of Ji and Yue remain forever unlike.

sentences.zh: 江左風味，盛道家之言，郭璞舉其靈變，許詢極其名理，仲文玄氣，猶不盡除，謝混情新，得名未盛。

translations.literal: The flavor of the Jiangzuo era abounded in Daoist discourse—Guo Pu exemplified spiritual transformation, Xu Xun pushed name-principle to its limit; Yin Zhongwen's mystical air was not wholly dispelled, and Xie Hun's fresh sentiment had not yet gained full renown.
translations.idiomatic: The taste of the Jiangzuo age overflowed with Daoist speech—Guo Pu embodied spiritual transformation, Xu Xun carried name-principle to its extreme; Yin Zhongwen's dark ether was not wholly cleared away, and Xie Hun's fresh feeling had not yet won wide fame.

sentences.zh: 顏、謝竝起，乃各擅奇，休、鮑後出，咸亦標世。

translations.literal: Yan and Xie rose together, each claiming singular excellence; Xie and Bao came later, both likewise marking their age.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and Xie rose together, each possessing a singular brilliance; Tiao and Bao came later, both likewise setting the mark of their age.

sentences.zh: 朱藍共妍，不相祖述。

translations.literal: Crimson and indigo each lovely—neither simply imitating the other.
translations.idiomatic: Crimson and indigo each beautiful—neither merely following the other's example.

sentences.zh: 今之文章，作者雖衆，總而爲論，略有三體。

translations.literal: Among writings today, though authors are many, taken together there are roughly three styles.
translations.idiomatic: In writing today, though authors are many, considered as a whole there are roughly three styles.

sentences.zh: 一則啓心閑繹，託辭華曠，雖存巧綺，終致迂回。

translations.literal: First: the heart opened in leisurely elaboration, language entrusted to splendid amplitude—though artifice and ornament remain, the result is ultimately circuitous.
translations.idiomatic: First: the heart opened in leisurely unfolding, language placed in splendid breadth—though clever ornament remains, the end is roundabout.

sentences.zh: 宜登公宴，本非准的。

translations.literal: Fit for grand feasts—it was never truly the standard.
translations.idiomatic: It suits grand public banquets; it was never truly the mark to aim at.

sentences.zh: 而疏慢闡緩，膏肓之病，典正可採，酷不入情。

translations.literal: Yet its slackness, looseness, and prolixity are maladies in the marrow—the canonical and correct may be mined from it, but it utterly fails to move the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yet its looseness, laxity, and lingering pace are sickness in the marrow—what is canonical and correct may be gathered from it, but it cruelly fails to enter the feelings.

sentences.zh: 此體之源，出靈運而成也。

translations.literal: The source of this style emerged from Xie Lingyun and took shape.
translations.idiomatic: The source of this style issued from Xie Lingyun and took form.

sentences.zh: 次則緝事比類，非對不發，博物可嘉，職成拘制。

translations.literal: Second: gathering facts and comparing categories—no statement unless in paired contrast; erudition is admirable but the craft becomes constraining.
translations.idiomatic: Second: assembling matters and comparing categories—nothing is uttered except in paired contrast; breadth of learning is admirable, but the craft ends in constraint.

sentences.zh: 或全借古語，用申今情，崎嶇牽引，直爲偶說。

translations.literal: Sometimes borrowing entire ancient phrases to express present feeling—tortuously dragging them in, it becomes mere paired talk.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes whole ancient phrases are borrowed to voice present feeling—dragged in by tortuous routes, it becomes nothing but paired talk.

sentences.zh: 唯睹事例，頓失清采。

translations.literal: One sees only examples and instantly loses clarity and color.
translations.idiomatic: One sees only instances and at once loses clarity and luster.

sentences.zh: 此則傅咸五經，應璩指事，雖不全似，可以類從。

translations.literal: This resembles Fu Xian's "Five Classics" and Ying Qu's topical pieces—not wholly alike, but of the same kind.
translations.idiomatic: This resembles Fu Xian's "Five Classics" and Ying Qu's pointed pieces—though not wholly alike, it may be grouped with them.

sentences.zh: 次則發唱驚挺，操調險急，雕藻淫豔，傾炫心魂。

translations.literal: Third: the opening cry startles and thrusts upward; the tonal handling is perilous and urgent; carved ornament is excessive and seductive—it dazzles and overturns the soul.
translations.idiomatic: Third: the opening note startles and shoots upward; tonal handling is perilous and urgent; carved ornament is lush and seductive—it overturns and dazzles the soul.

sentences.zh: 亦猶五色之有紅紫，八音之有鄭、衞。

translations.literal: Like red and purple among the five colors, like Zheng and Wei among the eight tones.
translations.idiomatic: It is like red and purple among the five colors, like the music of Zheng and Wei among the eight tones.

sentences.zh: 斯鮑照之遺烈也。

translations.literal: This is the surviving fierceness of Bao Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: This is the surviving fire of Bao Zhao.

sentences.zh: 三體之外，請試妄談。

translations.literal: Beyond these three styles, permit me a presumptuous word.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond these three styles, allow me to speak presumptuously.

sentences.zh: 若夫委自天機，參之史傳，應思悱來，勿先構聚。

translations.literal: If one entrusts oneself to heaven's mechanism, consults histories and annals, responds when thought presses from within—do not first assemble and construct.
translations.idiomatic: If one yields to heaven's mechanism, consults histories and annals, and answers when thought presses inward—do not first build and gather.

sentences.zh: 言尚易了，文憎過意，吐石含金，滋潤婉切。

translations.literal: Language should be easy to grasp; writing abhors excess of meaning—stones spit gold, moistening and refining with gentle sharpness.
translations.idiomatic: Words should be easy to finish; writing hates meaning pushed too far—spitting stone that holds gold, rich, smooth, and delicately incisive.

sentences.zh: 雜以風謠，輕脣利吻，不雅不俗，獨中胷懷。

translations.literal: Mix in folk ballads—light lips and nimble tongue; neither lofty nor vulgar, striking straight to the breast.
translations.idiomatic: Blend in folk songs—light lips and a nimble tongue; neither refined nor coarse, hitting the mark within the breast alone.

sentences.zh: 輪扁斲輪，言之未盡，文人談士，罕或兼工。

translations.literal: Like Wheelwright Bian carving wheels—the words never fully reach it; men of letters and talkers of doctrine rarely excel at both.
translations.idiomatic: Like Wheelwright Bian carving wheels—what is said never fully reaches it; literary men and disputants in doctrine rarely master both.

sentences.zh: 非唯識有不周，道實相妨，談家所習，理勝其辭，就此求文，終然翳奪。

translations.literal: It is not merely that knowledge falls short—the ways truly obstruct each other; what disputants practice makes reason overpower their words; seeking writing from this, in the end the writing is eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: It is not only that understanding is incomplete—the paths truly hinder one another; what disputants practice makes principle overpower their language, and if one seeks writing from this, in the end writing is obscured.

sentences.zh: 故兼之者鮮矣。

translations.literal: Thus those who combine both are rare.
translations.idiomatic: Thus those who unite both are few.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：學亞生知，多識前仁。

translations.literal: Encomium: Learning approaches inborn knowing; broad knowledge of sages past.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: Learning approaches inborn knowing; one knows many worthies of old.

sentences.zh: 文成筆下。

translations.literal: When writing takes form beneath the brush—
translations.idiomatic: When writing takes shape beneath the brush—

sentences.zh: 芬藻麗春。

translations.literal: Fragrant ornament rivals spring.
translations.idiomatic: Fragrant ornament rivals spring.

translations.idiomatic: Section divider.
